articleTitle: Sum Throughput Maximization in IRS-Aided Multigroup SWIPT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper studies the wireless multigroup network which is composed of a base station (BS), an access point (AP) and an N-element intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) to implement simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT). BS broadcasts wireless energy to several groups of internet of things (IoT) devices with direct/reflecting link in the downlink transmission, and the IoT devices will similarly transfer the obtained information for AP in the uplink transmission. To maximize the sum throughput, we develop an optimization problem jointly optimizing the bandwidth, the time slots and the reflecting phase shift matrices. Since these variables are strongly coupled together, an alternating optimization (AO) based algorithm has been stated for conducting its non-convexity. First, the lagrangian function and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions are adopted to derive both the optimal bandwidth and the wireless information transfer (WIT) time slots allocation. Then, the Lambert <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{W}$</tex> function is utilized to carry out the optimal wireless energy transfer (WET) time slot. Finally, the sub-optimal phase shift matrices are calculated in an iterative manner applying alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Simulation results validate that our proposed algorithm significantly outperforms the other benchmark schemes.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless information and power transfer

articleTitle: Direction Finding Method in Harmonic Amplitude with One-Bit Time Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The direction-finding method based on harmonic amplitude is established via a two-element time-modulated array (TMA) system, where the one-bit modulation scheme is utilized to reshape the distribution of the harmonic energy. By using such a scheme, the frequency interval between adjacent harmonics is expanded to the twice of the modulation frequency. The principle of the direction-finding system relies on establishing a mathematical relationship between the ratio of harmonic amplitudes and incident angles. By introducing the time delay in the modulation scheme, the amplitude ratio of harmonics will correspond to two values of incident angle, resulting in the limited scope of angular observation. To address the problem, two sets of relationships between amplitude ratios and angle are introduced to distinguish the ambiguous angle, where the value of the time delay is of importance. Numeric simulation results demonstrate that with a suitable choice of time delay under a one-bit modulated scheme, the direction-finding system can obtain correct estimation results across the full scope of the angle.

articleTitle: A Communication Protocol Identification Method Based on Time-Frequency Domain Combination for Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: At present, Internet of Things (IoT) testing instruments and meters are unable to identify the communication protocol of communication data when all characteristic parameters of communication data are unknown. Regarding this problem, this paper utilizes the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) model in machine learning, designs communication protocol identification methods and proposes a communication protocol identification method based on time-frequency domain combination (CPI- TFC). First, we generate time-domain waveforms and frequency-domain waveforms from sampling communication data sequences, and attempt only time-domain identification method and only frequency-domain identification method based on KNN model. Then, we compare the results, design a communication protocol identification method based on the combination of time-domain identification and frequency domain identification, and propose CPI-TFC. Experimental results show that CPI-TFC can achieve higher identification accuracy than only time-domain identification method and only frequency-domain identification method, so it can effectively identify the communication protocol for a IoT communication data. Moreover, CPI- TFC can provide prior information for subsequent configuring parameters in IoT testing instruments, improve the parameter configuration efficiency.

articleTitle: Joint Resource Allocation and Trajectory Planning for UAV-assisted Space-air-ground-sea Integrated Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In the Space-air-ground-sea integrated network (SAGSIN), Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are extensively utilized for reliable long-distance data transmission. Unlike traditional static relays, mobile relays enhance downlink per-formance through data-driven trajectory planning. This study jointly optimizes UAV trajectory, user scheduling, and power allocation to maximize the average transmission rate for multiple users in SAGSIN, ensuring overall system quality. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces UAV communication system energy consumption and enhances network throughput compared to traditional OFDMA schemes. These findings indicate that the algorithm has practical applications for improving communication efficiency in SAGSIN environments.

articleTitle: AoI-Oriented Information Freshness Performance Analysis in Maritime Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With growing interest in the maritime internet of things (MIoT), the information timeliness, serving as a crucial safeguard for the efficiency of sensory data acquisition and transmission, has garnered extensive research attention. However, the impact of marine environmental characteristics on information timeliness remains to be analyzed. Additionally, MIoT often employs relay vessel (RV) and multi-user access to expand communication coverage, but the effects of such factors on information timeliness are unclear. This paper presents a theoretical analysis of information timeliness in MIoT, using age of information (AoI) as the key metric. The marine sparsity is analyzed from two perspectives: sparse scattering and sparse user distribution, and a maritime communication model is established. A multi-source tandem queuing model is constructed to describe the data transmission process, then an analytical expression for the average AoI is derived to assess the impacts of RV sand multi-user interference on information freshness. Furthermore, approximate solutions for coverage probability and expected data rate performance are developed. Simulation results confirm the accuracy of the analysis.

articleTitle: RDAS-RFFI: Robust Differentiable Architecture Search for Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) identifies hardware devices by recognizing the subtle errors that inevitably occur during device manufacture. Most of the existing methods rely on the hand-tuning of parameters by experts, which makes it difficult to obtain high-accuracy networks quickly. In this paper, we proposed a robust differentiable architecture search for radio frequency fingerprint identification (RDAS-RFFI) method that introduces neural architecture search (NAS) to automatically obtain an effective neural network applicable to all signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), especially low SNR. First, we shrink the search space by retaining only three key operations. Second, we incorporate data augmentation techniques in search evaluation to enhance the robustness of the neural network. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RDAS-RFFI method outperforms the traditional manual design approaches, obtaining higher recognition accuracy with fewer parameters. Especially under low SNR conditions, RDAS-RFFI achieved significantly better performance.

articleTitle: Diffusion-Based Wireless Semantic Communication for VR Image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The vision of 6G includes numerous requirements for virtual reality (VR). This presents a significant data transmission challenge and demands substantial communication resources. Moreover, within the VR industry, data capture, stitching, and transmission often occur as separate stages, potentially diminishing the efficiency of the end - to-end communication process for VR images. This paper presents a novel semantic communication system for transmitting images captured by VR back-to-back dual-fisheye panoramic cameras. This system allows for the direct reconstruction of stitched panoramic images at the receiver, integrating the stitching process with semantic communication to enhance efficiency. Our method is called Diffusion-Based Semantic Communication for VR Images (DSCVI). The system involves several main steps. First, the transmitter extracts semantic information from the image captured by dual-fisheye cameras. It then uses joint source-channel coding (JSCC) technology to extract the semantic information and overcome distortion caused by the noise channel. Next, the receiver recovers the semantic information and controls the diffusion model to generate a stitched panoramic image. Our scheme is evaluated on the CROSS dataset and compared with the traditional methods. The results show that DSCVI generally surpasses the traditional methods in terms of quality metrics.

articleTitle: Research on End-to-End Delay Measurement Analysis Path in 5G Network Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: At the same time of the rapid expansion of 5G networks, the precise quantification of end-to-end delay is still a major problem restricting the improvement of business fluency and user satisfaction. To address this challenge, this study integrates advanced QoS Monitoring technology to achieve fine delay measurement from user equipment (UE) to user plane function (UPF), ensuring the delay transparency of the initial data transmission segment. Further, the DPI intelligent probe technology is used to analyze and measure the transmission delay from UPF to the main service station, and effectively fill the delay monitoring blind spot in the core part of the network. Combined with these two key technologies, the overall delay performance in 5G environment is comprehensively evaluated to achieve end-to-end delay measurement analysis.

articleTitle: A Transformer Based Signal Detection Method for Orthogonal Time Frequency Space Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) is an emerging modulation technique designed for high-speed mobile communication environments, which can effectively process signals in the delay-Doppler domain. However, OTFS faces some challenges in practice. One challenge which is emergent to address is the low robustness and high complexity of the existing signal detection methods. To this end, this paper proposes a joint channel estimation and signal detection scheme based on transformer neural networks. The proposed method achieves channel estimation and signal detection by fitting the input-output relationship of delay-Doppler (DD) domain signals without explicit channel state information (CSI). Simulation results show that the proposed transformer based approach can outperform existing methods, especially at high Doppler frequency shifts and multipath effects, which demonstrates the potential of deep learning for signal detection in OTFS systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Connectivity Optimization Algorithm in Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication reuses the spectrum resources of the cellular network, which can not only provide unrestricted information transmission between vehicles, but also improve the spectrum utilization efficiency. However, it also brings uncontrollable co-channel interference, which can not guarantee the quality of service of V2V communication. In order to reduce the interference of communication between vehicles and improve the overall connectivity of Vehicular Ad-Hoc Network (VANET). In this paper, we combine the Heterogeneous Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (HAPPO) algorithm with mean field theory (MFT) to propose a joint sub channel selection and power control algorithm, which improves the stability of V2V communication by reducing co-channel interference while maintaining stable overall performance. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the V2V communication connectivity and reduce the packet loss rate compared with the existing methods.

articleTitle: Research on Pattern Design of Integrated Sensing and Communication Reference Signal in 6G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), as an emerging technology, has the ability to further extend the potential application scenarios of 5G, and is considered as one of the 6G candidate technologies in recent years. In this paper, we investigate the pattern design of ISAC reference signal based on 5G physical layer protocols. Specifically, the effects of the time-frequency domain density and uniformity on the distance-velocity estimation are analysed. On this basis, an accuracy improvement scheme based on zero padding is proposed and validated in a radar simulator test environment. The relationship between signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), computational complexity and estimation accuracy is then demonstrated. Finally, some conclusions are drawn for future pattern design of ISAC.

articleTitle: FlexCP: Standard-Compatible Flexible Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: More and more attention is being drawn into standardization for integrating sensing and communications (ISAC) in 5G-A/6G. The functionalities of the future radio interface are extending from communications to sensing in the upcoming standardization. Given the compatibility issues, cyclic prefix orthogonal frequency division multiplex (CP-OFDM) waveform is one of the primary candidates in the 5G-A/6G standardization. However, one of the critical problems with CP-OFDM sensing is the fixed sensing coverage brought by limited CP options in current standardization. When the delay of the target echoes exceeds the length of CP, the resulting received signal will suffer from inter-symbol-interference (ISI) and inter-carrier-interference (ICI), which degrades the sensing performance. A standard-compatible CP extension paradigm is in demand. In this paper, FlexCP is proposed to enable flexible sensing coverage without introducing new frame structure into NR. With tone reservation in previous OFDM symbol, FlexCP extends the CP duration of the sensing OFDM symbol with preservation of communications resources in the extender symbol. Compared with standard CP options, FlexCP offers target sensing with larger detection range. Moreover, FlexCP can help subspace algorithms such as MUSIC achieving better performance for long-range targets. Simulation results depict enhancements in both detection range and multi-target resolvable range. Moreover, the power of the new designed symbol could be reduced as the original symbol as 1/3 of the reserved tone are used, leaving 2/3 of the subcarriers saved for communications purpose.

articleTitle: Sum-Throughput Optimization for VLC-Assisted UAV Networks with NOMA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The application of visible light communications (VLC) to unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) could achieve flexible and stable data transmission in 6G due to its advantages of high efficiency and intelligence. In this paper, firstly, we construct a VLC-assisted UAV network and introduce non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) to improve energy efficiency. Secondly, we propose a new power allocation strategy for NOMA VLC-UAV networks, aiming at the sum-throughput optimization (STO) subject to users' quality of service, illumination requirements, eye safety and transmission power limits, where the imperfect successive interference cancellation is considered for the first time. After that, the original non-convex problem is solved through the optimization theory and CVX tools. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy can significantly improve the network capacity and user reception performance, regardless of the presence of residual interference at the receiver.

articleTitle: Swin Kansformer-Based Semantic Communication Systems for Wireless Image Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of wireless communication technology, numerous applications are gaining increasing popularity, driving the quest for more efficient and innovative semantic communication frameworks. In this paper, we investigate a semantic communication architecture specifically designed for wireless image transmission. We redesign Swin Transformer (SwinT) and propose a new architecture called Swin Kansformer (SwinK) to facilitate the semantic feature transmission of images. Specifically, we implement the Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN), which excels in nonlinear activation optimization, and leverage it to redesign a semantic Unet-like network for image reconstruction tasks. By combining the Swin Transformer's powerful feature extraction capabilities and the KAN network's superior optimization performance, SwinK significantly enhances the quality and efficiency of image transmission. Finally, extensive simulation experiments demonstrate that the SwinK semantic communication architecture attains better performance for transmission efficiency and reconstruction quality in wireless semantic communication. The SwinK architecture shows outstanding potential and application prospects in addressing complex wireless communication environments, providing new ideas and directions for future wireless wireless communication development. On the CIFAR10 dataset, SwinK outperforms the wireless image transmission transformer algorithm (WITT) and the CNN-based joint source and channel coding network (JSCC). With a grid size of 10, our method achieves a 3dB improvement in PSNR at low SNR and a 5dB improvement at high SNR, along with a 1 % enhancement in MS-SSIM.

articleTitle: High-Accuracy Fault Diagnosis for SRv6 TE Policy in Computer Power Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the rapid development of communication networks, Computer Power Networks (CPN) hold promising prospects for 6G and future networks, and SRv6 network applications are becoming increasingly widespread. Network operators are placing greater emphasis on network operations and maintenance to enhance user experience. Fault diagnosis is a critical aspect of SRv6 network maintenance. Existing methods heavily rely on fault samples and are unable to achieve efficient and intelligent fault diagnosis in the presence of a large amount of unlabeled data. This paper combines unsupervised learning and supervised learning to reduce the dependency on labeled data, thereby avoiding the issue of intelligent maintenance being hampered by the scarcity of fault samples and adapting to in-creasingly complex communication network scenarios. Compared with traditional methods, this approach reduces the costly data labeling process. Simulation results show that the fault diagnosis accuracy of this method reaches 99.08%. Our method improves efficiency, reduces operational expenditures, and manages complexity, thus aiding in the automation and sustainability of SRv6 networks. This is of significant importance for the application of CPN in 6G and future networks, providing a reliable technical guarantee for the intelligent maintenance of networks.

articleTitle: Analysis of 6G Potential Use Cases and Service Requirements in 3GPP
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) is responsible for developing technical specifications for mobile communication systems. Global research into technologies to support the next generation mobile communication system has begun, and 3GPP is beginning to study 6G specifications. Firstly, this paper gives an overview of 3GPP and its general standardization procedure. Then, the views from the 3GPP Stage-1 workshop on IMT-2030 (6G) Use Cases are introduced and summarized. Five common 6G drivers are derived from global interest, including security and resilience, artificial intelligence (AI), immersive communication, sustainability, and ubiquitous coverage. Subsequently, use cases and their corresponding requirements are introduced for each of the common drivers. Finally, conclusions are given regarding the suggestions for the standardization work for 6G.

articleTitle: Elite GA Based 3D Deployment of Multiple UAVs for Maximum Coverage in IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Current ground base stations (GBSs) are facing unprecedented capacity pressure due to the increasing number of devices in the Internet of Things (IoT). Unmanned aerial vehicle base stations (UAV-BSs) can be deployed to provide on-demand services for ground users (GUs). In this paper, we propose a 3D deployment algorithm subject to the UAV-BSs' connection capacity limit and the connectivity requirements limit among UAV-BSs, maximizing the coverage GUs by UAV-BSs. Firstly, the k-means algorithm and elite genetic algorithm (EGA) are used to determine the optimal horizontal position of each UAV-BS under actual constraints. Next, the connections between the UAV-BSs and the GUs are updated based on the proposed fairness strategy. Finally, a height optimization algorithm is designed to optimize the deployment height of each UAV-BS based on the optimal elevation angle between the UAV-BS and the GU. Simulation results show that the proposed 3D deployment algorithm achieves higher coverage for GUs through 3D deployment of multiple UAV-BSs, ensuring the robustness of the UAV-BS network.

articleTitle: Securing Crowdsourced Localization to Resist Attack Based on Service Security Value Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The location information of nodes is increasingly crucial across various IoT services, given the expanding application diversity and node numbers within the Internet of Things. crowdsourced localization can decompose complex localization tasks into many anchor nodes to solve jointly. However, crowdsourced localization accuracy depends on anchor nodes' reliability. The localization performance cannot be guaranteed in the presence of attacks. This paper proposes a novel localization scheme to resist attacks based on service security value evaluation. Firstly, this paper proposes a concept of service security value of anchor nodes (SSoA) to evaluate their reliability. Secondly, based on SSoA, a collaborative node selection strategy was designed. The security localization effect has been significantly improved by selecting more reliable anchor nodes to participate in localization. Finally, the strategy and algorithm proposed in this paper were validated through simulation, and the results showed that the scheme can resist attacks and achieve accurate localization.

articleTitle: Mask Learning Enabled Multi-Rate Text Semantic Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based semantic communication has been deemed a promising communication paradigm to break through the bottleneck of traditional communications. However, most of the existing research focuses on designing semantic communication systems with a fixed rate, which is inflexible and inefficient for practical dynamic scenarios. To address this problem, this paper proposes a mask learning enabled multi-rate text semantic communication (MMSC) scheme. Specifically, by incorporating the target rate as side information, a lightweight rate-aware attention module is developed to improve the DL model's adaptability. Then, an effective feature masking method with learnable padding is proposed, wherein a padding-related regularization loss is designed to assist the recovery of the masked symbols. Through end-to-end mask learning, arbitrary rates with high semantic recovery performance can be achieved. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MMSC scheme outper-forms the other multi-rate semantic communication methods in terms of bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU) score.

articleTitle: Development of Robotic Arm Digital Twins via Edge-to-End Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper establishes a digital twin model for a single robotic arm manufacturing unit based on edge-end archi-tecture and modifies the robotic arm for wireless communication, enabling it to read and write data via the edge computer. The paper details the software and hardware configuration, as well as the communication architecture, and conducts latency tests for reading and writing the robotic arm using different communication methods. By using complex motion trajectories calculated at the edge, the trajectory control of the robotic arm was achieved. The results demonstrate that the robotic arm manufacturing unit based on edge-end architecture is highly feasible, with wireless transmission latency close to that of wired transmission. This lays a foundation for the digital twinning and swarm control of future robotic cluster manufacturing workshops.

articleTitle: Enhancing Virtual Coupling Train Sets Communication via Generative Diffusion Models: A Data-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Virtually Coupled Train Sets (VCTS) represent an emerging control system for modern railways, which, through the use of train-to-train (T2T) communication, promises dynamic coupling and more efficient scheduling in the future. Despite the benefits, VCTS wireless communication faces challenges due to dynamic network structures and variable communication needs, affecting performance and reliability. This study introduces a Generative Diffusion Models (GDMs)-based data-driven method to enhance VCTS wireless communication. We created an expert dataset using an iterative random shooting method, capturing optimal strategies for specific conditions. The GDMs was trained on this dataset to map environmental states to effective communication strategies, tailored to VCTS's unique dynamics. Our method not only mimics expert strategies but also expands the strategy space to adapt to system demands. Simulations show that GDMs outperforms traditional methods in data rate and reliability, demonstrating its adaptability and robustness across network configurations. We discuss the benefits and challenges of GDMs and propose future research directions. This research presents a novel approach to optimizing VCTS wireless communication and broadens the application of GDMs in complex networks.

articleTitle: Rate Maximization in Sweeping Robot-Assisted Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted communication is recognized as a promising technology in academia and industry because it offers a novel and promising solution for implementing both secure and good-quality wireless communication networks. The paper proposes installing an RIS on a sweeping robot to act as the mobile passive relay, which can flexibly deploy the location of RIS and enhance communication capacity. In this paper, the maximization problem of user throughput is formulated, and we jointly optimize transmission power at AP and reflection phase shifts at RIS. It is difficult to deal with the optimization problem. Therefore, we separate the two variables into two subproblems, i.e., the transmit power optimization problem and the reflection phase-shift optimization problem. We can solve these problems by semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and alternating optimization algorithms. The simulation results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed algorithm, which enhances the communication capacity efficiently.

articleTitle: Direction-of-Arrival Estimation with Efficient Graph Spatial Spectrum Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Existing graph signal processing (GSP) based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation methods suffer from high computational complexity due to the way of graph spatial spectrum construction. In this paper, an efficient GSP-based DOA estimation method is proposed by incorporating a new cost function to construct the graph spatial spectrum. By per-forming the graph Fourier transform on the received signals that are represented with a weighted directed graph, the graph frequency spectrum are obtained and analyzed, from which a cost function is developed allowing efficient graph spatial spectrum construction. Then, the DOA is estimated by searching for peaks in the constructed graph spatial spectrum. Simulation results demonstrate improved estimation accuracy and efficiency compared to existing GSP-based DOA methods.

articleTitle: A Collaborative D2D Authentication Method Based on Traffic Fingerprinting for Future Power Private Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: To address the problem of efficient security authentication for power private networks, this paper proposes a D2D collaborative authentication method for terminal devices based on traffic fingerprinting. The method extracts feature information by analysing and identifying the traffic data generated by the terminal devices of the electric power wireless private network. We introduces D2D technology to facilitate collaborative authentication among terminal devices. Meanwhile, an attention mechanism is introduced to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the authentication. The simulation results show that the proposed method based on attention mechanism and ensemble learning can improve the accuracy of terminal device authentication.

articleTitle: Unmanned Ship Tracking Algorithm Based on MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the rapid development and widespread application of autonomous unmanned systems, the application scenarios of unmanned ships in maritime traffic are also expanding. However, this also brings hidden dangers to navigation safety and maritime traffic safety. In order to reduce the occurrence of maritime accidents, it is particularly important to improve the perception ability of unmanned ships of target information in the surrounding environment, especially the information of moving targets. This paper proposes an unmanned ship tracking algorithm based on MIMO radar to solve the problem of real-time tracking of surrounding moving targets by unmanned ships in a marine environment with impulse noise characteristics. This study uses the multi-input and multi-output characteristics of MIMO radar, combines the maximum correntropy criterion and the projected approximate subspace tracking (PAST) algorithm to estimate the feature vector in the impulse noise environment, and then combines the estimation of signal parameters via invariance techniques (ESPRIT) algorithm to accurately estimate the target's direction of departure (DOD) and direction of arrival (DOA), and proposes the MCC-PAST-ESPRIT algorithm. The simulation experimental results show that compared with the PAST-ESPRIT algorithm which is based on the minimum mean square error criterion, the method proposed in this paper shows better robustness and accuracy in the impulse noise environment.

articleTitle: Efficient Latency Optimization in Batch Processing Server Systems for Multi-User Co-Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the progression of internet of things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI), the demand for real-time, high-performance edge computing in multi-user collaborative inference scenarios has intensified. Batch-processing edge servers play a pivotal role in optimizing resource allocation, throughput, and overall system performance. This paper delves into the utilization of servers equipped with batch processing capabilities in edge computing for multi-user collaborative inference contexts. The inference tasks are partitioned into sub-tasks, and the minimization of user latency under energy consumption constraints is investigated. Initially, we assume a constant inference latency for the edge server and propose an iterative algorithm that explores partition points. Additionally, we introduce a traversal algorithm for the largest batch (TALB), taking into account the actual latency of the edge server. These algorithms demonstrate a significant reduction in task processing latencies of up to 79.5 % and enhance system performance across various conditions, particularly in scenarios with limited server bandwidth or significant capability differences among user devices.

articleTitle: Hop-Based High-Value Information Underwater Wireless Sensor Routing Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks (UWSNs) have been widely applied in fields such as ocean monitoring and military operations. However, due to the complexity of underwater acoustic channels, the Depth-Based Routing (DBR) protocol faces significant challenges in addressing the void problem. Specifically, the greedy selection of nodes with the smallest depth in DBR can achieve local optimization but not global optimization. High Value of Information (VoI) data cannot be reliably transmitted to the sink node, resulting in high energy consumption and low delivery rates. Therefore, this paper proposes an improved DBR routing protocol driven by high information value. Firstly, hop counts are deployed throughout the network. Secondly, an optimal routing mechanism based on hop count and depth is designed. Finally, extensive experimental simulations demonstrate that the proposed routing protocol outperforms other underwater routing protocols in terms of performance.

articleTitle: MIMO Radar Phase-Coded Waveform Design for Spectrum Sharing: A Neural Network Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Spectrum sharing technology significantly enhance the utilization of radio frequency (RF) spectrum resource in radar and communication systems. MIMO radar has higher degrees of freedom in transmitting notched waveforms and is more likely to coexist with in band users. Unlike traditional optimization algorithms, this paper utilizes a neural network to address spectral constrained waveform design problem. Based on the proposed solution mapping network (SMN), unsupervised learning is employed to minimize a weighted sum of waveform orthogonality metrics and spectrum metric. Numerical results demonstrate that this network effectively designs waveforms with spectral notches while maintaining high waveform orthogonality.

articleTitle: Shift-Based Symmetric Coprime Planar Arrays for Direction Finding with Enhanced Uniform Degrees of Freedom
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Recently, sparse planar arrays have attracted significant attention due to its advantage in underdetermined two-dimensional (2-D) direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. In this paper, we propose a novel sparse planar array configuration called shift-based symmetric coprime planar array (SSCPA), leveraging the difference co-array (DCA) technique to generate a large virtual array with increased number of uniform degrees of freedom (uDOFs). The closed-form expression of the number of uDOFs is then derived, and compared with existing structures. Simulation results confirm that superior performance in terms of resolution capacity and estimation performance is achieved by the proposed structure.

articleTitle: An Improved Kriging Algorithm for Spatial Variability in Wi-Fi Fingerprint Positioning Database Construction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In Wi-Fi fingerprinting location, constructing traditional fingerprint databases consumes a large amount of human resources. Interpolation algorithms are typically used to reduce the workload of database construction, and the Kriging algorithm is a widely used interpolation algorithm. However, existing algorithms do not consider the nonlinear variation in received signal strength indication (RSSI) in free space. In this paper, an improved Kriging algorithm based on spatial variability is proposed by analysing the propagation law of electromagnetic waves in free space, separating the regions with drastic and slow changes in RSSI, and then fitting a semivariance function to the two regions for interpolation. Through real simulation tests, the proposed algorithm has demonstrated improvements in interpolation accuracy, achieving gains of approximately 4.6 % and 8.1 % over traditional Kriging and the Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) algorithm, respectively. The interpolation accuracy of the proposed algorithm is superior to both Kriging and IDW algorithms, effectively enhancing localization precision, making it more suitable for constructing an RSSI fingerprint database.

articleTitle: Detecting Ranging Spoofing Attacks on IEEE 802.15.4z
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the development of wireless sensing, both accuracy and privacy issues have gained much attention from industry to academia. Short range plays a role in sensing field, and in precision ranging the Impulse Radio Ultra-Wideband (IR-UWB) is widely adopted primarily due to its high temporal resolution. The IEEE 802.15.4 group has especially set UWB physical layer (PHY) for precision ranging. In the latest standard IEEE 802.15.4z, the scrambled timestamp sequence (STS) field has been added to improve the security of ranging. However, it is still vulnerable to PHY attacks, such as Ghost Peak and Cicada\Cicada++ attack. These spoofing attacks introduce distance reduction, sometimes be fatal in practice. In this paper, we propose a consistency check scheme (CCS) to detect spoofing attacks. Based on the special structure of STS, we calculate both segment-based estimates and STS-based estimate. The scheme checks the consistency of these two types of estimates. If all differences are less than the consistency threshold, we judge that no spoofing attacks exist in current ranging process and the final estimated distance is equal to the STS-based estimate. If any difference exceeds the threshold, a spoofing attack is detected and we conclude the ranging environment is insecure and invalid all estimates. Taking Ghost Peak as an example, simulation results show that the scheme is an effective method to detect spoofing attacks.

articleTitle: Radar-Based Non-Contact Blood Pressure Estimation Using Multi-Dimentional Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper presents a non-contact blood pressure (BP) estimation method by using the biomedical radar sensor. The carotid pulse wave signal is acquired by the LFMCW radar sensor. Then the multi-dimensional features are derived from the radar-acquired pulse wave signal. A CNN model has been utilized for BP estimation. The mean absolute errors of systolic BP and diastolic BP are 4.72 mmHg and 3.31 mmHg, respectively. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed BP estimation method.

articleTitle: Delay-Minimization and Load-Balancing Task Offloading in Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: As an emerging computing paradigm, Mobile edge computing (MEC) can provide more efficient and flexible computing services for the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). However, due to the dispersed deployment locations of computing nodes, the varying service requirements of tasks, and the complexity of wireless transmission environments, efficient task offloading in IIoT remains an important issue. In this paper, we investigate the problem of task offloading and resource allocation in a multi-computing node collaboration scenario. A joint resource allocation, offloading nodes, and paths selection optimization (JRNP) algorithm is proposed to minimize the total task completion latency, the maximum node load, and the maximum network link load. The original problem is decomposed into sub-problems by the proposed algorithm, which are optimized alternatively. Furthermore, a heuristic algorithm is developed to address the task offloading decision sub-problem by integrating the cache constraints of the nodes, the network load, and the performance of multi-hop links. Simulation results illustrate that the proposed algorithms can effectively balance the network load and significantly reduce the total task completion delay.

articleTitle: eVTOL Communication and Trajectory Optimization in Low-Altitude Economy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The low-altitude economy relies on developing Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing Vehicle (eVTOL) industries, wherein safe aviation and efficient communication are critical features of these e VTOLs. The safe and efficient operation of low altitude economy requires all e VTOLs to fly in the predetermined paths. However, a predetermined path may be very complicated in practice. Maintaining formation and efficient aerial communication on complex predetermined paths is challenging for eVTOL. To address the problem, a composite artificial potential field (APF)-based trajectory and communication optimization scheme is proposed for e VTOL aviation, enabling efficient communication and predetermined trajectory flight. This paper devises a composite APF that comprises four potential fields, i.e., communication, target, separation, and alignment APF. The composite APF comprehensively engages the effects of communication, formation, and predetermined routes, and has sufficient parameters to fully control the flight of e VTOL. To optimize the composite APF-based flight control, we develop a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) that can generate a safe and communication-efficient e VTOL flight along the complex predetermined path.

articleTitle: Zero-Power Backscatter Sensing and Communication Proof-of-Concept
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we present an experimental setup to evaluate the performance of a radio frequency identification (RFID)-based integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system. We focus on both the communication and sensing capabilities of the system. Our experiments evaluate the system's performance in various channel fading scenarios and with different substrate materials, including wood, plastic, wall, and glass. Additionally, we utilize radio tomographic imaging (RTI) to detect human motion by analyzing received signal strength indicator (RSSI) data. Our results demonstrate the impact of different materials and environments on RSSI and highlight the potential of RFID-based systems for effective sensing and communication in diverse applications.

articleTitle: Distributed Resource Allocation Mechanism for NOMA-Integrated V2X Toward 6G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The integration of New Radio (NR) V2X and Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) can further optimise sys-tem communication efficiency, which can be a game changer for sidelink in upcoming 6G V2X systems. Moreover, in NR-V2X Mode 2, vehicles are required to sense channel status autonomously without resource scheduling of base station (BS), which could result in inefficient utilisation of communication resources. Consequently, we propose a group-cast NOMA-V2X communication model, regarding vehicles as independent individ-uals and developing distributed sub-channel and power allocation algorithms to solve the problem. Our approach comprises two stages. Firstly, in sub-channel allocation phase, a pricing-based switching algorithm is proposed to enhance system communication capacity. Secondly, for power control, we model the problem as a potential game and prove that Nash equilibrium exists. Subsequently, a Q-learning algorithm is proposed to achieve Nash equilibrium. Simulation results demonstrate that the algorithm is capable of converging and achieving a significant increase in system communication capacity.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of Massive Data Transfer for Super Intelligent Computing Service
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the development of super intelligent computing services, the requirement for massive data transfer (MDT) across long distance networks from edge data centers/enterprises to core data centers continues to increase. The network operators are strongly demanded to provide high efficiency MDT between the large-scales super intelligent computing centers. However, the conventional MDT scheme are achieved by manual express, which the valuable data suffer from security and damage risks. In this paper, we propose a low cost and highly efficient MDT scheme based on TCP for existing IP networks. To maximize the MDT rate and network bandwidth utilization, the TCP parameters are optimized. The performance of two congestion control algorithms, such as cubic and bbr, are studied in our experiment. The field experiments are also demonstrated to verify the MDT performance. The experiential results show that up to 9.18 Gbit/s MDT rate is achieved in a 1400 km field experiment with a 10 Gbit/s link rate. Moreover, it is worth noting that the proposed MDT scheme presents lower cost, higher efficiency, and flexibility for new supercomputing and intelligent computing services.

articleTitle: Learning Interpretable Phase Difference Mapping for Scalable DOA Estimation via Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Interpretability is the major bottleneck regarding the deep learning-based direction of arrival estimation (DL-DOA). This paper provides novel insight into the mapping relationship (MR) for DL-DOA, which can be interpreted as a mapping from the received signal to the spatial phase difference (SPD) with prior information of array geometry (AG). Based on the learned MR, two scalable DL-DOA methods are developed. One method refers to the variability of AG, enabling the trained model to be utilized for varying AGs without the requirement of retraining network. The other involves scaled resolution (SR) by using an equivalent finer grid, which significantly mitigates the problem of grid mismatch for off-grid DOA with a coarse pre-defined grid. The efficacy of proposed methods is demonstrated through simulations with different network structures. The code for this work is available at: https://github.com/hslcode/DOA-Scalable.

articleTitle: Low-Overhead Pilot Pattern and MUSIC-Based Channel Estimation for OTFS Systems with Doppler Squint Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation has been regarded as one of the most promising candidates to enhance communication reliability for emerging high-mobility applications, where channel estimation is a crucial component to exploit the performance superiority. Unfortunately, most prior estimators fail to work under extremely high mobility since the Doppler squint effect is ignored. Additionally, traditional schemes suffer from high pilot overhead due to the extensive guard symbols required to prevent interference between data and pilot symbols in the delay-Doppler domain. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel pilot pattern in the time-frequency domain, significantly improving the transmission efficiency. A multiple signal classification-based estimator is then developed to extract channel parameters. Simulation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed estimator.

articleTitle: A Low-Complexity Expectation Propagation Detector for MIMO-OTFS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modu-lation has been demonstrated to achieve reliable communication over time-varying wireless channels in high-speed dynamic environments. In this paper, the expectation propagation (EP) algorithm is employed for signal detection in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-OTFS systems, aiming to enhance de-tection reliability compared to linear minimum mean square error and message passing approaches. By exploiting the sparsity of the time-domain matrix, the computational complexity of matrix inversion in the iterative process of the EP algorithm is reduced. A time-domain EP detection algorithm with log-linear order complexity is proposed. Numerical experiments validate that the proposed receiver achieves a bit error rate performance comparable to traditional EP receivers while maintaining lower computational complexity.

articleTitle: A Maximum Flow Algorithm Based on Undirected Storage Time Aggregated Graph for Unmanned Surface Vessel Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: An Undirected Storage Time Aggregated Graph (US TAG) model is proposed for solving the maximum flow problem in Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) networks. Considering the time-varying characteristics of USTAG, we propose an augmenting path seeking method based on Breadth First Search (BFS) and design a method to calculate the maximum flow of the augmenting path as well as update the residual network. The case study shows that the proposed algorithm can effectively solve the maximum flow of time-varying USV networks.

articleTitle: Active Power Control for Off-Shore Wind Turbines Against FDI Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Recently, offshore wind power has rapidly developed due to its low environmental interference and abundant wind resources. However, due to its remote geographical location and high demand for communication infrastructure, off-shore wind turbines (OWTs) are vulnerable to potential threats from false data injection (FDI) attack. FDI attack can interfere with active power control strategies by tampering with the rotor speed data measured by sensors and pose a threat to the stability of the power grid. To ensure that OWTs can accurately track the active power instructions set by wind farm's control center under FDI attack, this paper proposes a rotor speed control (RSC) strategy based on Kalman filtering technology (RSC- KF). This strategy can estimate the rotor speed of the wind turbine in real-time, and then a residual detection and compensation mechanism is designed to effectively detect and correct attacked rotor speed information caused by FDI attack. Further, based on the corrected rotor speed, the RSC method is developed, which can flexibly switch control strategies according to different rotor speed values, ensuring the efficient operation of OWTs under different wind speed conditions. The proposed approach's effectiveness is proved via simulations conducted on the OpenFAST platform.

articleTitle: WSN Coverage Optimization Based on Improved Lion Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: After the random deployment of wireless sensor nodes, issues such as overlapping coverage and detection blind spots inevitably arise. Employing intelligent optimization algorithms to optimize node deployment and expand network coverage is a common approach. However, the high-dimensional optimization problem of sensor node deployment and the complexity of coverage areas make it difficult for conventional intelligent optimization algorithms to achieve satisfactory solutions. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a wireless sensor network coverage optimization scheme based on a Lion Swarm Optimization (LSO) algorithm with a crisscross strategy. By introducing both horizontal and vertical crisscrosses of individuals during the population evolution process, the diversity of the population is increased, enhancing the algorithm's global search capability and ability to escape local optima. Results demonstrate that the improved LSO algorithm exhibits enhanced solution accuracy and convergence compared to the standard LSO algorithm. In the context of wireless sensor network coverage optimization, this algorithm provides a better design solution.

articleTitle: A Non-orthogonal Multi-carrier Frequency Hopping Based Secure Differential Chaos Shift Keying for Autonomous Ummanned Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Secure information transmission is of great significance for the long-term safe and stable operation of autonomous unmanned systems. Based on a new non-orthogonal multi-carrier modulation technology and the idea of frequency hopping modulation, a non-orthogonal multi-carrier frequency hopping Differential Chaos Shift Keying secure communication technology is proposed in this paper. The improvement of system confidentiality is mainly reflected in three aspects. Firstly, the initial value sensitivity of chaotic sequences ensures the complexity of sequences. Secondly, non-orthogonal multi-carrier modulation can make the subcarriers need not follow the strict orthogonality between them, so that the frequency interval is more flexible, which improves the spectrum utilization of the system while increasing the symbol complexity and the difficulty of decipher. Thirdly, the frequency hopping mechanism will further increase the system complexity and the difficulty of deciphering. In this paper, two non-orthogonal multi-carrier Differential Chaos Shift Keying systems with frequency-hopping mechanism are proposed, the system structure and the modulation and demodulation principle of the two systems are described, and the BER performance and security performance of the system are studied by numerical simulation. At the same time, the superiority of the proposed system is verified by comparing with the current typical multi-carrier chaotic communication system.

articleTitle: Exploration on Potential Applications of ProSe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The ProSe scheme proposed by 3GPP aims to provide a low-cost coverage extension method, which is based on the adjacent D2D communication mode, not only providing a connection service, but also supporting multiple business scenarios and building multiple commercial services. Therefore, this paper explores how to build Prose application ecology, so as to better apply ProSe to real life. This paper focuses on the analysis of the application types of ProSe and the analysis of the actual application scenarios of ProSe. Finally, it introduces the consideration of the existing problems and puts forward the corresponding suggestions.

articleTitle: A Low-Bits Quantized Error Feedback Based Downlink Beamforming Iteration Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Transceiver with a multi-antenna structure could achieve the spatial freedom of the transmission channel, and it has been widely used in many wireless applications. The transmitting power could be concentrated within a narrow beam width so that both the security and electronic environment sensing ability are improved by suitable downlink beamforming. However, there are always some mismatches between the beamforming weights and actual downlink channel, so the optimal reception performance and sensing accuracy are hard to be achieved. Some training methods have been proposed, but their effectiveness is always subject to the transceiver structure and system duplex model. In this paper, we propose a low-bits quantized error feedback based downlink beamforming method. By using the feedback information and first-order perturbation analysis, an approximate gradient for the leaked components minimization and a downlink beamforming iteration are given successively. The weight is easily updated by the previous beam, signal and feedback on legal user, and there is no need for the receiver to known the codebook.

articleTitle: Research on Temperature Rise of Doubly-Fed Asynchronous Air-Cooled Wind-Driven Generator Based on Simulation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In order to quickly evaluate the temperature rise of the generator under different working conditions and predict whether maintenance is needed, this article analyzes the main factors affecting the temperature rise of air-cooled wind-driven generator, and proposes a prediction method for generator temperature rise. This method can be used to evaluate the temperature rise of the generator under different environments, altitudes, and other conditions. At the same time, it can also evaluate whether the generator will overheat when the power increases based on the current operating situation of the wind-driven generator, and make early warnings and maintenance. This article takes the 8.5MW doubly fed asynchronous air-cooled wind-driven generator as the research object, and the accuracy of theoretical calculations is determined by comparing the results of numerical simulation and fluid-structure coupling simulation analysis with the results of theoretical prediction.

Author Keywords: doubly fed asynchronous air-cooled wind-driven generator

articleTitle: The Resource Management Architecture of 5G NPN Network Based on Fuzzy Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Mobile communication networks will become more integrated with industries as 5G technology advances, and new kinds of industry needs will keep emerging. Vertical industries represented by low-latency, high-reliability, and large-scale machine-type communication services need to provide customized and innovative service applications. In this paper, we focus on the network requirements of thousands of industries in Non-Public Network (NPN), categorize the end-to-end bandwidth, delay, jitter, packet loss rate and other SLA indicators of customized network through fuzzy mathematics, quantify the network performance indicators and user requirements using fuzzy logic, and make decisions based on fuzzy rules to achieve more accurate SLA management, and provide a flexible network adaptation foundation to create a sound and innovative service application for exploring a variety of new business models. Flexible network adaptation foundation to create benign network self-intelligence capabilities.

articleTitle: Deep Over-the-Air Computation Based Multi-User Semantic Communication for Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Aided by IoT and AI technologies, the rapid development of smart cities has imposed higher transmission and computation demands on wireless communication systems. This paper introduces SC-DAC, an innovative multi-user semantic communication framework leveraging deep over-the-air computation (AirComp) to address these challenges. SC- DAC merges communication and computation via a deep AirComp encoder, enabling the utilization of the superposition of multiple access channels. This integration allows for the fusion of multi-user information during transmission and eliminates the necessity for multi-user detection at the receiver. Additionally, to optimize task outcomes, the semantic encoders, decoders, and AirComp encoder are jointly fine-tuned. Simulation results indicate that as the number of users increases, system performance remains relatively stable and shows promise in efficient resource utilization. What's more, when applied to the AI-based tasks such as multi-user multi-modal action recognition, SC-DAC enhances the accuracy of action recognition by 26 % compared with traditional methods and by about 30%-50% compared with other multi-user semantic communication methods under conditions of low SNR. The scheme where data is transmitted in an error-free channel serves as an upper bound.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Spectrum Prediction Using Combined Model for Power Wireless Private Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Power wireless private networks could optimize the resource allocation by predicting the future spectrum state, thus improving the reliability and stability of communications. This paper proposes a deep combination model-based multi-band spectrum prediction method for power wireless private networks. First, this paper uses variational mode decomposition (VMD) to decompose the original sequence into several intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), which can significantly reduce the impact of high data volatility. Then, the osprey optimization algorithm (OOA) is used to optimize the hyper-parameters of the long short-term memory (LSTM) module. A dual-attention mechanism is adopted instead of a single-attention mechanism to allow the model to better focus on the important parts and optimize the prediction results. The experimental results show that the proposed deep combination model exhibits better performance in multi-band spectrum prediction tasks on real spectrum datasets.

articleTitle: Identification and Classification of 5G-R Interference Signals: A Transformer-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Accurate identification and classification of 5G-R interference signals are crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of railway communications. This paper proposes a novel approach for the 5th Generation Mobile Communication Technology-Railway(5G-R) interference signal identification and classification utilizing the transformer model. In our scheme, a data preprocessing technique called Locally Weighted Scatterplot Smoothing (LOWESS) is employed to mitigate the effects of noise in the sample spectrum, thus enhancing the model's recognition accuracy. The proposed transformer model, renowned for its exceptional performance in sequence processing tasks, leverages its self-attention mechanism to effectively capture the intricate patterns within the interference signals. Through comparative simulations involving the convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) models, the results demonstrate that the proposed transformer model achieves superior performance in identifying and classifying 5G-R interference signals.

articleTitle: Optimal Column Inversion Precoding for PAPR Reduction in SP-OTFS System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) systems often encounter challenges associated with significant peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) and excessive out-of-band (OOB) power radiation, which leads to deteriorate the overall communication system's performance. Although precoding techniques implemented at the transmitter can effectively mitigate OOB radiation, the challenge of high PAPR remains unresolved. To address this issue, a novel approach named optimal column inversion precoding (OCIP) is introduced. This algorithm outputs a column reversal precoding matrix that exhibits the lowest PAPR among potential candidates. Notably, OCIP preserves the orthogonality of the precoding matrix, which means that the suppression of OOB radiation remains same with spectrally precoded OTFS (SP-OTFS) systems. Simulation results indicate that OCIP is highly effective in PAPR reduction with maintaining same OOB and bit error rate (BER) performance of the SP-OTFS system.

articleTitle: Bridging Beam Split and Semantic Communications: Enhancing Transmission Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper proposes an image semantic communication scheme that utilizes entropy-based ordering under beam split transmission conditions, named BSISC. Based on the entropy model, the BSISC scheme matches semantic features of varying importance, encoded through joint source-channel coding, with the fading channels produced by beam splitting. This enhances the quality of information recovery. The BSISC scheme is expanded to a dual-user scenario, resulting in the mBSISC scheme. The mBSISC scheme can serve two users simultaneously through channel multiplexing technology based on channel differentiation, ensuring the presence of the main beam lobes without mutual interference. The mBSISC scheme effectively improves resource utilization efficiency and ensures the quality of information recovery for two users. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed BSISC significantly outperforms methods without entropy-based ordering in terms of the peak signal-to-noise ratio of the received images. Moreover, mBSISC can serve two users simultaneously while guaranteeing recover quality.

articleTitle: Secure Task Offloading of UAV Assisted Offshore Edge Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Offshore edge networks face the risk of malicious eavesdropping in the process of offloading computational tasks from nodes to edge servers, and it is difficult to ensure the efficiency and security of task computation offloading. In this paper, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) are introduced as offshore relay nodes to assist in the safe offloading of tasks, and the task offloading rate and UAV relay hovering position are optimised so as to prevent the occurrence of malicious eavesdropping and improve the security of the task offloading process. Simulation results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the size of the node eavesdropping data volume, and improve the computational efficiency of the network task offloading at the same time. The proposed method also reduces the energy consumption of UAV by optimising the hovering position and trajectory of UAV, and realises the safe task offloading under the offshore edge network based on the assistance of the Relay UAV (R-UAV).

articleTitle: Optimizing the Consensus Algorithm of Blockchain in the Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, a blockchain consensus algorithm tailored to Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environment is proposed to solve the deficiencies of traditional consensus algorithms such as high latency, low throughput and excessive resource consumption. The proposed approach adopts a hybrid consensus algorithm, which combines the Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS) algorithm with the Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) algorithm. This hybrid algorithm elects representative nodes via a voting mechanism to execute the verification process. Simulation results demonstrate that the consensus algorithm delineated in this paper outperforms traditional consensus algorithms in terms of latency and throughput, rendering it better suited for IoV-related scenarios.

articleTitle: FedLSTM Based Cooperative Weather Prediction in RAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In regions such as Botswana, where agriculture, water resources, and public safety are heavily impacted by variable climates and extreme weather, intelligent weather forecasting is indispensable. This research introduces an advanced Federated Long Short-Term Memory (FedLSTM) model, integrated with Radio Access Network (RAN) technology, to enhance intelligent data analytics capabilities across dispersed weather stations. The integration of RAN facilitates not only secure and efficient data transfers but also enables intelligent, real-time data processing at multiple nodes. This decentralized approach to machine learning harnesses the power of collective intelligence from multiple data sources, significantly improving the precision and localization of weather forecasts. The use of intelligent data analytics in this context helps to overcome traditional limitations such as data scarcity and computational constraints, allowing for the synthesis of diverse geographical and climatic data. Experimental results demonstrate that the FedLSTM framework, supported by smart data analytic techniques and RAN, achieves a remarkable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> score of 97 %. This confirms the model's enhanced capability to accurately predict weather patterns, showcasing its effectiveness in deploying intelligent solutions to complex weather forecasting challenges.

articleTitle: Edge and Terminal Cooperation Enabled LLM Deployment Optimization in Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the remarkable emer-gence of large language models (LLMs), demonstrating exceptional capabilities in handling complex tasks such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing. However, the prevalent deployment of LLMs on cloud servers poses challenges in ensuring user data privacy and minimizing computation and transmission delay. Moreover, LLM needs to read all the parameters to generate a token for each inference and then splices the original input with the generated token as a new input to generate the next token. To address these concerns, we propose a novel LLM deployment framework leveraging edge and terminal cooperation. Our proposed framework involves deploying LLMs on both edge server and terminal device, where the LLM model on the terminal generates tokens serially, while the model on the edge generates tokens in parallel. This edge-terminal cooperative and serial and parallel combination framework can effectively reduce the computation delay of token generation. To further optimize the performance of the proposed framework, we formulate an optimization problem aimed at minimizing average delay and energy consumption. Considering its integer programming property, we employ a branch and bound algorithm to efficiently solve this problem. Extensive simulation results provide compelling evidence of the effectiveness of our LLM deployment optimization algorithm. Under diverse channel conditions and terminal device computing capabilities, our proposed scheme consistently outperforms other baseline algorithms in terms of delay and energy consumption. These findings underscore the potential of our approach in facilitating the practical deployment of LLMs on edge and terminal.

articleTitle: Secret and Covert Communications for Multi-Antenna Uplink UAV Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, a joint wiretap and covert transmission method is proposed for uplink multi-user multi-antenna ground to unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications. To characterize the fundamental limit of the above scenario, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the sum of secret and covert transmission rates subject to constraints of secrecy outage probability (SOP), detection error probability (DEP), and the transmit powers of secret and covert transmitters. To solve the optimization problem, we propose a bisection search algorithm using semidefinite relaxation and reveal the influence of key parameters on the wiretap and covert transmission rates, analytically and numerically. Our results fill the gaps in joint wiretap and covert transmission for uplink multi-user multi-antenna UAV communications and provide new insights to construct such systems.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Minimizing for Fixed-Wing UAV Inspection Systems with Kinematic Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a flight energy consumption model (FECM) for fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) under the consideration of the UAV flight rate, turn radius and heading changes. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed FECM, we study a UAV-based urdan environment patrol inspection system, where a fixed-wing UAV flies subject to kinematic and safety constrains. We aim to minimize the total energy consumption of UAV by jointly optimizing the UAV turn radius, frequency of heading change and inspection sequence. Due to the nonlinearity of the constraints and the nature of the combinatorial optimization problem, the formulated problem is non-convex, making it challenging to obtain its optimal solution. To tackle this issue, we decompose the original problem into two subproblems: 1) trajectory design between adjacent inspection points; and 2) optimal the patrol sequence among cruise points. An improved hybrid A* algorithm (IHA*A) is proposed to determine the optimal trajectory. Then we optimize the patrol sequence by genetic algorithm (GA) to determine the optimal traverse order. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly reduces energy consumption compared to the baseline scheme.

articleTitle: Movable-Antenna Array Empowered ISAC Systems for Low-Altitude Economy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper investigates a movable-antenna (MA) array empowered integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) over low-altitude platform (LAP) system to support low-altitude economy (LAE) applications. In the considered system, an un-manned aerial vehicle (UAV) is dispatched to hover in the air, working as the UAV-enabled LAP (ULAP) to provide information transmission and sensing simultaneously for LAE applications. To improve the throughput capacity and meet the requirement of the sensing beampattern threshold, we formulate a data rate max-imization problem by jointly optimizing the transmit information and sensing beamforming, and the antenna positions of the MA array. Since the data rate maximization problem is non-convex with highly coupled variables, we propose an efficient alternation optimization based algorithm, which iteratively optimizes parts of the variables while fixing the others. Numerical results show the superiority of the proposed MA array-based scheme in terms of the achievable data rate and beamforming gain compared with two benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based LOS and NLOS Parameters Estimation, Tracking, and Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems have large bandwidths and, combined with large-scale antenna arrays and beamforming technology, facilitate higher resolution of angle and delay measurements. This, in turn, provides opportunities for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). Accurate and reliable estimation of mmWave channel state information is crucial for ISAC. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based method for estimating channel multipath parameters, tracking, and identifying line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) paths. Specifically, we leverage a network named “you only look once (YOLO)”, a highly efficient object detection network in computer vision, to detect the angles of arrival (AOAs) and angles of departure (AODs) of multipaths from received radio frequency signals. Moreover, we use a tracking-by-detection algorithm, ByteTrack, to track the variation of each path's AOA and AOD under a mobile scenario. Thanks to these vision-based channel estimation approaches, we reveal that LOS and NLOS paths exhibit different trajectory properties, allowing us to precisely identify LOS and NLOS paths, a challenge originally in the context of ISAC. We validate the proposed estimation, tracking, and identification methods on real measurement data and demonstrate that the proposed estimation method shows better performance compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Multi-Base Station Radio Map Prediction Based on Residual Enhanced Dual Path UNet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Radio maps are used for various applications such as resource allocation, interference control, fingerprint positioning, and network planning. With the development of 5G and subse-quent mobile communication technologies, establishing detailed radio maps has become crucial to effectively utilize limited spec-trum resources. Traditional methods for constructing radio maps typically rely on complex physical models and environmental parameters, resulting in time-consuming and computationally in-tensive processes. Although some machine learning methods have been proposed to construct radio maps, their accuracy still needs improvement.
