This paper proposes a novel radio map prediction method based on Residual Enhanced Dual Path UNet (RED-UNet), an improved version of RadioUNet. By adding residual connections and batch normalization after each convolutional layer, RED-UNet accelerates model convergence, enhances model generalization, promotes gradient flow, and mitigates gradient disappearance, thereby improving the accuracy of radio map prediction. Additionally, we utilize this method for predicting radio maps in areas of interest containing multiple base stations. Compared to traditional prediction methods, our method demonstrates better accuracy. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Environmental Cognition-Driven Hierarchical Decision-Making for Air-Ground Collaborative Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The unparalleled communication and sensing capabilities of the 6th generation (6G) networks can fulfill the diverse requirements of emerging scenarios like the metaverse. However, several issues such as queue transmission between numerous heterogeneous nodes and difficulties in understanding complex and dynamic environments from high-level cognition urgently need to be addressed. In response, this paper proposes an environmental cognition-driven method based on graph convolutional networks (GCNs), which comprehensively considers node positions, task queues, and frequency conflicts, then optimizing node clustering to cope with complex and dynamic electromagnetic environments. In the meanwhile, to overcome the limitations of conventional reinforcement learning (RL) methods in addressing the increasing complexities of multi-task and multi-granularity decision-making, a hierarchical reinforcement learning (HRL) method based on the actor-critic (AC) framework is proposed to quick decision-making for air-ground collaborative communication. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed environmental cognition-driven hierarchical decision-making method can reduce redundant interactions among nodes and improve the transmission rate.

articleTitle: Sensing-Assisted End-to-End Beamforming Based on Reinforcement Learning in LEO Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper proposes a sensing-aided end-to-end channel prediction and beamforming scheme based on reinforcement learning (RL) for multi-user communication systems in low earth orbit (LEO) satellite scenario. In case of channel non-reciprocity, the base station (BS) can directly use the uplink pilot information to complete the downlink beam design and data transmission. To improve the efficiency of channel prediction, by exploiting the features of integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) system, this paper uses the estimated angle-of-arrival (AoA) information as prior knowledge to enhance the self-learning efficiency of the channel prediction network. Simulation results show that the end-to-end channel prediction and beamforming scheme effectively enhances the system's transmission efficiency while reducing time overhead.

articleTitle: Beamforming Design for Secure MC-NOMA Empowered ISAC Systems with an Active Eve
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: As the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology emerges as a promising component of sixth-generation (6G), the study of its physical layer security has become a key concern for researchers. Specifically, in this work, we focus on the security issues over a multi-carrier (MC)-non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) assisted ISAC system, considering imperfect channel state information (CSI) of an active Eve and graded confidentiality demands for users. To this end, the sub carrier allocation, the information, and artificial noise beamforming are designed to maximize the minimum communication rate, while ensuring diverse confidentiality and sensing performance demands. An effective security strategy is devised via the Lagrangian dual transformation and successive convex approximation methods. Simulations confirm the validity and robustness of the proposed scheme in terms of the security performance.

articleTitle: Improved Chaotic Modulation Encrypting Method for Uplink Multi-User Massive MIMO Systems with Large-Scale Fading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In the coming sixth generation (6G) wireless communications, uplink multiuser massive multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) systems face serious physical layer security risks. Using chaos theory to generate keys on the modulation information is an effective encryption method for single-input and single-output and small-scale MIMO systems. However, due to large-scale antennas located in massive MIMO systems, more enormous uplink crosstalk interference resulted in much higher bit error rate (BER) for the traditional chaotic modulation encryption methods than those of unencrypted signals, especially in the large-scale fading cases Thus, in this paper, we propose an improved chaotic modulation encrypted algorithm and its corresponding decryption method for the uplink multiuser large-scale faded massive MIMO systems. The closed form expression of the theoretical lower bounds on the BER performance for the maximum likelihood detection algorithm for the proposed encrypted signals is analyzed. The simulation results verified its correctness. The proposed encrypted signals can not be recognized by the eavesdropper. The BERs performance of the proposed encrypted method approach the theoretical lower bounds of the optimum ones, and are much better than those of the traditional chaotic encrypted method in uplink massive MIMO systems with large-scale fading. The proposed encrypted method has a medium/strong robustness against different large-scale fading or channel estimation error.

articleTitle: On the Physical-Layer Security of RSMA-Based UAV Communications with Imperfect CSI Over Nakagami-$m$ Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this work, we propose a scheme for providing secure communications in low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks by employing rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) in the presence of a passive eavesdropper. The UAV acts as an aerial base station and serves multiple terrestrial users. We investigate the secrecy performance in terms of secrecy outage probability and ergodic secrecy rate under channel state information estimation errors over Nakagami-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m$</tex> fading channels. Numerical results corroborate the accuracy of the derived analytical expressions and indicate that the proposed RSMA scheme has superior secrecy performance compared to other conventional multiple access schemes.

articleTitle: Symbol Detection of Ambient Backscatter Communication Systems in High- Mobility Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Ambient backscatter communication exploits the ambient radio frequency signals as the carrier to reduce the system battery and hardware costs, positioning it as a promising solution for the large-scale deployment of future Internet of Things networks. In high-speed mobile environments, the channel undergoes time-frequency selective fading, posing significant challenges for tag information transmission. To address this issue, we propose using orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation within the ambient backscatter system, transforming the doubly-selective fading channel into a relatively quasi-static delay-Doppler domain for processing. In addition, we propose embedding the tag information in the selection of the combi-nation of modulated frequencies. However, the tag's frequency modulated signals are closely coupled with channels, making it challenging to extract tag information from the unknown channel state information (CSI). To tackle this problem, we then propose an off-grid SBL-based method to obtain tag symbols from the highly structured equivalent CSI. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Real-Time Routing Design for LEO Satellite Networks: An Enhanced Multi-Agent DRL Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks have been heralded as a promising solution for provisioning space-based Internet services. However, the inherent dynamic topology, characterized by frequent variations in inter-satellite link states, causes pronounced fluctuations in latency and exacerbated packet loss rates. To address the challenge, in this paper, we formulate a routing design and optimization problem to maximize the average throughput with considering the end-to-end latency constraint and the real-time routing demand in LEO satellite networks. To solve this problem, we design an enhanced Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) algorithm, which encapsulates the intricate interplay among LEO satellite agents and their environs within a Real-Time Markov Decision Process (RTMDP) framework, and introduces the self-attention mech-anism to endow agents with a better grasp of environmental state dynamics. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed routing design outperforms the benchmark schemes in terms of both end-to-end latency and network average throughput.

articleTitle: A Physical Layer Security Algorithm for IRS-Assisted MIMO Communication Networks via GDM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In wireless communication networks, Intelligent Re-flective Surfaces (IRS) can amplify the signal gain for legitimate users and diminish the correlation between the primary and eavesdropping channels, thereby improving network security. To optimize the physical layer security (PLS) in a multi-user Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) channel with a multi-antenna eavesdropper, a non-convex programming problem is formulated. This problem involves jointly optimizing the base station (BS) beamforming matrix and the IRS phase shift matrix. The objective is to maximize the minimum achievable secrecy rate. The Generalized Diffusion Model (GDM) algorithm is employed to enhance the interaction capability of the generated solution with the environment. Simulation experiments demonstrate that increasing the number of IRS array elements and array antennas in IRS-assisted MIMO communication networks can improve network security. Specifically, there is an improvement of 16.02% in the minimum secrecy rate compared to the benchmark algorithm of Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG).

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient Beam Hopping Strategy in Interference Coexistence Satellite Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: While beam hopping (BH) has revolutionized satel-lite communication by addressing non-uniform traffic demands and minimizing beam interference, existing research on multi-satellite BH scenarios often overlooks energy efficiency (EE) optimization. This can lead to increased operational costs and reduced satellite lifespans due to higher onboard energy consumption. In this paper, we propose a novel energy-efficient beam hopping strategy in the coexistence scenario of geosynchronous orbit (GSO) and non-geosynchronous orbit (NGSO) satellite systems. Specifically, the proposed strategy can both balance traffic load among NGSO satellites and avoid interference to GSO ground stations. A joint multi-satellite BH optimization problem is formulated to optimize a trade-off function between quality of service (QoS) and EE for the NGSO system. Then, the original problem is divided into the satellite-cell assignment, BH pattern design, and beam power allocation sub-problems and solved sequentially. The numerical results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed strategy in enhancing the QoS and EE of the NGSO system while effectively mitigating interference with the GSO system.

articleTitle: Leveraging Angular Feature for RIS-Assisted Positioning Over Dynamic Multipath Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper investigates reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted fingerprint positioning in a dynamic scattering-rich environment. We use the RIS to passively sense multipath characteristics and improve the positioning performance. A novel fingerprint named the angular-spatial fingerprint (ASF) is proposed for user positioning. Compared with the conventional received signal strength (RSS) fingerprint, the ASF describes the multipath angle of arrival (AoA) information between the user and the RIS and therefore has better multipath adaptability and stability. As the RIS is a passive component, the ASF is difficult to obtain directly. Based on angle-domain signal processing methods, we propose a low-cost method to capture the ASF by using the RIS. Then, a confidence factor-assist dynamic fingerprint training method is proposed to increase the robustness of positioning in changing environments. Finally, the location of the user is estimated via the weighted K-nearest neighbour (WKNN) method. Simulation results demonstrate the validity of the proposed method and show the potential of RISs in wireless positioning.

articleTitle: Service Fluctuation Mitigated Energy and Effective Computing Contract for Distributed Computing Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In the realm of distributed computing networks, managing service fluctuations and optimizing energy consumption are paramount challenges. This paper introduces the Service Fluctuation Mitigated Energy and Effective Computing Contract (SrvfmEECC), which is a novel framework designed to address these challenges. The SrvfmEECC provides two contracting models, including Full Time Contract (FTC) and Part Time Contract (PTC), for computing nodes (CNs) upon their integration into the network. The framework strategically distributes computing services (CSs) across CNs to mitigate service fluctuations and optimize energy efficiency. Innovative aspects of SrvfmEECC include an initial performance threshold evaluation, specialized monitoring for FTC nodes, and a dynamic task allocation algorithm that prioritizes task reuse, PTC CN preferences, and load balancing. Numerical analysis demonstrates that SrvfmEECC can reach superior total gain and energy savings, particularly in larger network scales. The proposed algorithm enhances operational efficiency and contributes to environmental sustainability, marking a significant advancement in distributed computing resource management.

articleTitle: Beamforming Design for RIS-Aided MIMO Communication: A Piece-Wise Near-Field Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This work proposes a joint active and passive beam-forming design for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided wireless communication systems. We adopt a piece-wise near-field channel model that leverages the benefits of the traditional near-field approach while enhancing its robustness against channel estimation errors (CEEs). We analyze the impact of different channel models, including the existing near-field, the proposed piece-wise near-field, and far-field channel models, on the interference distribution caused by CEEs and model mismatches. Then, by considering the interference as noise, we formulate a joint active and passive beamforming design problem to maximize the spectral efficiency (SE) and address it exploiting a block coordinate descent (BCD) framework. Simulation results demonstrate that adopting the piece-wise near-field channel model leads to an improved SE compared to both the traditional near-field and far-field models in the presence of CEEs. Additionally, the proposed piece-wise channel model strikes an effective balance between modeling accuracy and system degrees of freedom (DoF).

articleTitle: On the Combination of AI and Wireless Technologies: 3GPP Standardization Progress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Combing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and wireless communication technologies has become one of the major tech-nologies trends towards 2030. This includes using AI to improve the efficiency of the wireless transmission and supporting AI deployment with wireless networks. In this article, the latest progress of the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) standards development is introduced. Concentrating on AI model distributed transfer and AI for Beam Management (BM) with wireless network, we introduce the latest studies and explain how the existing standards should be modified to incorporate the results from academia.

articleTitle: Exploiting Active Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface in Secure Communication System for Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) have become a significant technology to improve the wireless propagation environment. Besides, the physical layer security is also a paramount metric in future communication systems. Since the double path loss exists in the reflection link, the performance of deploying RIS in wireless communication system has been limited. In this study, we delve into the active RIS-assisted secure multiple input single output (MISO) system in the presence of a single eavesdropper (Eve). Our main purpose is to optimize the system's energy efficiency (EE) while maintaining the achievable rate at Eve blew a predefined threshold. To achieve this, the transmit beamforming and reflection matrix is refined alternately by employing quadratic transform and successive convex approximation (SCA) approach. Simulation results unveil that the proposed scheme can enhance energy efficiency more significantly than the benchmark schemes while secures the physical layer of the system.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimization for Resource-constrained Federated Learning in Large-scale IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Large-scale Internet-of- Things (IoT) networks enable intelligent applications and services, such as autonomous deriving. As many users generate various datasets, federated learning in distributed IoT networks emerges from learning from distinct datasets. To realize efficient and reliable communications in distributed networks, we propose a collaborative optimization model for resource-constrained federated learning using a joint design of wireless resource allocation and expected learning losses. Precisely, we start to formulate a learning-oriented power allocation problem. Then, we derive a convergence bound and build the relationship between communications and learning. At last, we perform an optimal algorithm based on majorization-minimization frameworks. Thanks to the high parallelization of the proposed algorithm, extensive experimental results corroborate that optimal power allocation in distributed networks benefits efficient federated learning compared to the state-of-the-art benchmark algorithms.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning based Edge Offloading Strategy for Port Infrastructure States Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: It is necessary to establish an edge computing system to provide computing power for latency sensitive monitoring data process task of port infrastructure states monitoring sys-tem. Considering the difference between power supply mode of onshore and offshore edge computing servers in port, an edge computing system architecture for port infrastructure monitoring is designed. The monitoring devices task offloading problem is formulated as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP), whose objective is minimizing the weighted-sum of latency and energy consumption with computing power and latency constraints. A Deep Deterministic policy gradient-based task Offloading and Computing resource allocation (DDOC) algorithm is proposed to solve the CMDP problem. Simulation results show that compared with other baseline solutions, the proposed DDOC effectively realized joint optimization of latency and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Adaptive Tompson Sampling for Beam Tracking in Terahertz Empowered Immersive Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Massive Multi-Input Single-Output (MISO) Tera-hertz (THz) communication is a promising technology that offers high throughput and low latency, meeting the demands for immersive communication experiences. Currently, most of the existing works in the THz MISO system require channel acquisition to obtain accurate channel state information (CSI), allowing the base station (BS) precoder to be adjusted for data transmission. However, the large number of antennas for a massive MISO communication system significantly increases the time needed for channel acquisition, resulting in substantial latency. This paper presents an adaptive Thompson sampling that utilizes previously acquired channel distribution to achieve high-rate transmission. Due to hardware limitations, adjusting the precoder for each transmitted symbol, as done in many current methods, is impractical. Instead, this paper proposes a new transmission strategy that configures the precoder for multiple symbols within each time block, considering both CSI acquisition and data transmission. By intelligently adjusting the precoder of the MISO BS, we demonstrate that the average transmission rate can be progressively increased. Simulation results show that the proposed adaptive Thompson sampling outperforms Sequential Selected Precoder and other state-of-the-art methods, improving the average transmission rate by at least 30%.

articleTitle: A Radio Map Approach for Antenna Pattern Calibration in Low-Altitude Air-to-Ground Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Reconstructing antenna radiation patterns typically requires specialized anechoic or reverberation chambers, which are costly and resource-intensive. This paper investigates the feasibility of using outdoor signal strength measurements to achieve the same goal. Current methods relying on controlled environments are less accessible for extensive use, often requiring sophisticated instruments. To address these limitations, we propose a approach that leverages sparse reference signal received power (RSRP) measurements to build a two-dimensional (2D) power angular map (PAM) of the antenna. Assuming horizontal isotropy of the antenna, the PAM is constructed with distances as column indices and elevation angles as row indices, capturing key characteristics of the antenna's radiation pattern. A weighted K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)-based matrix completion method is employed to impute missing values, followed by Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to separate antenna gain from path loss. Our experimental results, obtained through simulations and real-world measurements, demonstrate that only 30 elevation angle measurements are needed to achieve a normalized mean squared error (NMSE) of less than 0.01 for the reconstructed antenna pattern of a half-wave dipole antenna. Further validation using a UAV measurement system for the VERT 2450 antenna shows that the reconstructed radiation pattern has a similar distribution to that provided in the VERT 2450 datasheet, confirming the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Sparse Superimposed Codes for Vehicular Communications with Low-Resolution ADCs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Sparse superimposed codes (SSC) are a promising short-packet transmission scheme in next generation communication systems. This paper presents a quantized SSC (Q-SSC) based short-packet scheme for sensing data transmission in vehicular communication systems with low-resolution analog-to-digital converters. The core idea behind Q-SSC is to transmit short-packet data by mapping information bits to multiple superimposed sparse vectors. The superimposed sparse vectors are then mapped onto subcarriers for transmission after pseudo-random spreading. At the receiver, the decoding process is transformed into a sparse signal recovery problem, and a conjugate gradient hard thresholding pursuit algorithm is proposed for accurate decoding from quantized measurements. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed Q-SSC scheme outperforms existing schemes in terms of block error rate over doubly selective channels.

articleTitle: Robust Loosely Coupled SLAM System with LiDAR and IMU for Multi-Curve Dynamic Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the widespread development of ground mobile robot applications, high-precision localization and mapping capabilities have become crucial. In this paper, a loosely coupled localization and mapping system, PED-LOAM, based on Lidar and IMU is proposed. This system utilizes the high-precision pose output from Lidar odometry and combines IMU data to achieve accurate localization and mapping. Unlike most solutions based on the assumption of static objects to reduce the impact of dynamic environments on localization accuracy, this paper first employs the advanced ground segmentation method Patchwork++ for preprocessing. It then uses Iterated Error State Kalman Filter (IESKF) to fuse point cloud matching odometry data based on distance and normal vector constraints with IMU data. In the backend fine matching process, a method for dynamic point cloud removal is proposed. By removing sparsely dense point clouds and utilizing an iterative point cloud co-visibility approach, dynamic objects are eliminated for iterative matching, thereby outputting high-precision localization information. Testing on the KITTI and M2DGR datasets shows that, for the KITTI dataset, the average percentage improvement in ATE Root Mean Square Error over LEGO-LOAM is 42.48% and over the advanced algorithm LVI-SAM is 33.04%. In the M2DGR dataset testing, the average percentage improvement in ATE Root Mean Square Error over LEGO-LOAM is 73.97%, and over EKF-LOAM in terms of RPE is 28.34%. These results demonstrate that the localization capability of the PED-LOAM system is more robust and accurate.

articleTitle: Robust Max-Min SINR for Active RIS Aided Multiuser MISO System With Outage Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a robust precoding scheme in active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted mul-tiuser multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems, aiming to reduce the impact of inevitable transceiver hardware impairments (HWI) and imperfect channel state information (CSI) on communication performance. Specifically, the closed-form expression of the distorted noise power caused by transceiver HWI is derived to quantify HWI. Moreover, we develop a statistical CSI error model to characterize the imperfect CSI of the base station (BS)-RIS channel as well as the RIS-user channel and derive the CSI error distribution of the BS- RIS-user cascade channel. Further, we focus on the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) maximization problem, which considers the effects of the distortion noise and the outage constraints caused by the imperfect CSI. However, the minimum SINR maximization problem is challenging due to its non-convexity and non-closed form outage constraints. Therefore, we propose an algorithm combining the fractional programming (FP) method with the decomposition-based large deviation inequality (DBLDI) method to transform the outage constraints into closed-form constraints and then using the semi-definite relaxation (SDR) algorithm to deal with the resulting non-convex problem. Numerical results show that our algorithm can significantly improve the communication rate compared to existing algorithms and the proposed robust scheme has outperformance over the existing schemes.

articleTitle: Referential Task-Oriented Emergent Semantic Communications for Mobile Augmented Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: As mobile augmented reality (MAR) becomes integral to interacting with digital twins and the Metaverse, it demands stringent requirements in latency, computational efficiency, and energy conservation. Traditional methods leveraging edge, cloud computing, and 5G networks encounter considerable challenges, notably communication latency with visual data, which compromises the quality of experience (QoE). This paper presents an innovative semantic communication framework tailored for enhancing MAR applications. By adapting the Lewis signaling game, we train two agents to develop an efficient communication protocol, allowing the exchange of complex visual information via compact, meaningful messages. Unlike existing semantic communication models that emphasize data reconstruction, our approach prioritizes task completion, employing a discrete protocol optimized for referential tasks. To align with real-world scenarios, channel uncertainty is integrated into our training process. Experimental validations reveal that our method surpasses traditional semantic communications in referential task performance significantly, showcasing its potential for MAR applications while acknowledging the challenges of implementation. This work not only proposes a solution to a pressing problem in MAR but also opens avenues for future research in task-oriented communication.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Enabled Reverse Offloading in Cooperative Vehicle Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The advent of cooperative vehicle-infrastructure system (CVIS) has the potential to turn the futuristic transportation system into reality. Although CVIS can increase the road safety and traffic efficiency, it also brings the challenge of huge data processing demand. Fortunately, with reverse offloading, the soaring computing capabilities of connected autonomous vehicles (CAV s) can be utilized to address the limitation in computing power. In this paper, the reverse offloading strategy is adopted in a vehicular edge computing (VEC) network, aiming to reduce the system latency through intelligent task partition and resource allocation. Specifically, we firstly formulate the reverse offloading problem as a Markov decision process (MDP), considering the time-varying status of channel quality, task queueing status, and task load. Then, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm to learn optimal decisions by interacting with the environment. Specifically, a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) based algorithm is proposed to make task partition and allocation decisions in a constrained continuous manner with the help of Softmax function. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly reduce the system latency compared to three baseline schemes. Notably, when facing the longer traffic rush time, the advantages of the proposed method are progressively growlng.

articleTitle: Image Coding and Compression Method Based on Semantics of Pixels for Semantic Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Semantic image transmission is promising for both image reconstruction or downstream task execution. However, it is still challenging to simultaneously achieve pleasing visual clarity and superior downstream tasks. To tackle this issue, we propose a semantic-preserving image coding and compression method based on the semantics of pixels (SP). Specifically, we first project the semantic importance onto pixels, which is quantified by a gradient-based mechanism. Then, we design an SP-based loss function to train the image coding and compression network. This loss function not only preserves the semantic information to boost the performance of intelligent tasks but also preserves the pixel information to achieve pleasing visual effects. Experimental results confirm improvements in both aspects of performance. Especially for intelligent task performance, the proposed method achieves up to 22.22 % and 78.40 % performance gain ratio compared with the state of art deep learning-based and the traditional method, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Attack Surface Management Technologies and Telecom Operators' Strategies for Space-Air-Ground Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: While the new generation of communication technologies, such as satellite Internet and air Internet, are developing at a high speed, the continuously expanding attack surface also brings new security risks and challenges. Attack surface management can comprehensively understand the vulnerability and potential risks of the enterprise from the attacker's point of view, and help the organization to continuously improve the construction of the security system. This study firstly introduces the attack surface management framework and its development status, then analyzes the attack surface of Space-Air-Ground Networks, then compares the attack surface management technology with other security solutions, and finally proposes implementation strategies of attack surface management technology for Space-Air-Ground Network from the perspective of telecom operators.

articleTitle: Joint Task Offloading and Multi-Channel Access for Industrial Edge Computing: A Transformer-Based MADRL Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC) can efficiently address the concerns of insufficient computing resource of Indus-trial Devices (IDs) in emerging smart factories. However, limited communication resources pose challenges for heterogeneous in-dustrial tasks with different real-time requirements. In this paper, we first model the Task Offloading and Multi-Channel Access (TOMCA) problem as a graph structure based Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process. Then, to solve this problem, we design a transferable TOMCA (T2OMCA) algorithm based on Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL). The T2OMCA algorithm incorporates Transformer to handle the graph structure observations of IDs, which allows the algorithm to selectively focus on the features of heterogeneous tasks to learn better strategies. In addition, the T2OMCA algorithm is transferable, compensating for requirement of retraining previous MADRL algorithms with minor topology changes. The extensive simulations show that the T2OMCA algorithm outperforms existing algorithms in terms of both the average completion rate and the average processing delay of tasks with generalization for time-varying IWCNs topologies.

articleTitle: Source Localization Based on UAV Swarm Trajectory Optimization with Incomplete Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In complex urban environment, the source localization is hindered as sensors cannot simultaneously receive signals due to building occlusion, the phenomenon known as incomplete measurements, which could adversely affect the localization per-formance. In order to improve the accuracy of source localization, a technique based on the DAV swarm trajectory optimization is exploited in this paper. Firstly, the received signal strength (RSS) is utilized to obtain the rough estimation of the source to adjust the trajectory of UAV s. Secondly, by optimizing the UAV flight path, time difference of arrival (TDOA) and Doppler frequency shift (DFS) are employed to localize the source. Then, the non-convex problem is established by maximum likelihood (ML) and modified to the semi-definite relaxation (SDR). Finally, the source localization is obtained by solving the convex optimization problem. The proposed methods achieve superior performance over the existlng methods. as validated by using simulation.

articleTitle: Low-Latency Resource Allocation Scheme in OTFS-NOMA IoV Platoon System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Vehicle platoon-based communications are increasingly emerged in recent wireless communication systems. How-ever, low-latency communication for vehicular platoon systems has substantial hurdles because of the dynamic channel states, the complexity of practical road environments, and the high-mobility vehicles. A viable solution to these issues is non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) in Delay-Doppler (DD) domain, which increases spectrum efficiency and system capacity. In this paper, we investigate the internet of vehicle (IoV) platoon resource allocation for DD-domain based NOMA systems. To satisfy the quality of service (QoS) requirements for each vehicle, the optimization problem is first developed to allocate resources through the vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) links, including delay requirements, rate requirements, and power restrictions. Then, a decoupling tech-nique, known as the alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM), is used to solve the formulated non-convex optimization problem. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach satisfies QoS standards and considerably lowers system delay compared to baseline methods. In addition, the devised algorithm can lead to high computational efficiency in computing the formulated problem.

articleTitle: Distributed Radio Map Reconstruction Based on Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Radio maps (RMs) can provide valuable information about the wireless environment by describing the distribution of received signal strength (RSS) in physical space. In this paper, we propose a novel distributed RM online reconstruction scheme, where the client unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) collect RSS samples measured by mobile users for local model training, and a server UAV performs model aggregation to optimize the global model. Unfortunately, in practice, the measured RSS samples may be sparse, non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID), and there is heterogeneity among the client UAVs, making the reconstruction of the complete RM intractable. Therefore, we proposes a RM online reconstruction scheme based on semi-asynchronous federated learning (SAFL) and generative adversarial networks (GAN), where GAN is utilized to generate RMs from sparse and non-uniformly distributed RSS data. To address the challenges of non-IID RSS data and client heterogeneity, our scheme design a weight assignment algorithm based on the Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) and client model staleness degree. Simulation results demonstrate that, compared to conventional algorithms, the proposed algorithm significantly improves reconstruction accuracy and convergence speed thanks to these aforementioned design.

articleTitle: Beamforming Optimization for Sensing Result Fusion in Distributed ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we study the transmit and receive beamforming vectors in a distributed integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where a base station (BS) per-forms the downlink communication and active sensing tasks simultaneously. While reflected signals are utilized for passive sensing at the receive access points (RAPs). Due to the limited backhaul capacity between the central controller (CC) and RAPs, the BS and each RAP make independent decisions and transmit their binary inference results to the CC for result fusion. Furthermore, we explore two cases of the signal-to-interference- plus-noise ratio (SINR) for user equipments with and without the sensing interference cancellation. Subsequently, we aim to maximize sensing performance while meeting the minimum SINR requirements and the power budget at the BS. Finally, numerical results demonstrate that the proposed beamforming optimization scheme can reach the upper bound of performance and significantly outperforms the power optimization scheme utilizing fixed beamforming vectors.

articleTitle: Enabling Trustable Financing: A Verifiable Privacy-Preserving Cross-Chain Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Generative AI-enabled wireless communications enhance efficiency and offer new tools for supply chain finance (SCF) innovation. SCF optimizes capital efficiency and reduces risk, but information asymmetry hinders risk assessment. Blockchain technology addresses these challenges by solving information asymmetry and regulatory issues. However, issues of privacy protection, reliability, and traceability remain. To address this, we design a verifiable privacy protection cross-chain protocol based on threshold homomorphic encryption. This protocol ensures confidential sharing and verifiable access to enterprise information through homomorphic encryption and distributed private key technology, enhancing data security and controllability in SCF. Our simulation experiments demonstrate the protocol's feasibility and effectiveness in cross-chain SCF scenarios, supporting the application of blockchain technology in supply chain finance.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithm for Secure Communication in Space-Air-Ground-Sea Integrated Network via Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: To enhance communication security in the 6G Space-Air-Ground-Sea Integrated Network (SAGSAIN), we utilize distributed cooperative beamforming (DCB) with a virtual node antenna array (VNAA) to reduce signal strength in non-target directions. UAVs optimize their positions to minimize the maximum side lobe level (SLL) while balancing energy consumption. This study formulates a joint optimization problem targeting maximum SLL, secrecy rate, and UAV energy consumption, solved using the GAINB algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in improving the security of the system.

articleTitle: A DAFT Based Unified Waveform Design Framework for High-Mobility Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the increasing demand for multi-carrier communication in high-mobility scenarios, it is urgent to design new multi-carrier communication waveforms that can resist large delay-Doppler spreads. Various multi-carrier waveforms in the transform domain were proposed for the fast time-varying channels, including orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS), orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM), and affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM). Among these, the AFDM is a strong candidate for its low implementation complexity and ability to achieve optimal diversity. This paper unifies the waveforms based on the discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT) by using the chirp slope factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$k$</tex> in the time-frequency representation to construct a unified design framework for high-mobility communications. The design framework is employed to verify that the bit error rate performance of the DAFT-based waveform can be enhanced when the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is sufficiently high by adjusting the chirp slope factor k.

articleTitle: Comparison of OTFS and OFDM in High-Mobility Scenarios Based on Ray-Tracing Simulated Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The strong time variability of multipath channels in high-mobility scenarios causes the orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal to suffer from serious inter-carrier interference (ICI) and inter-symbol interference (ISI), resulting in performance degradation. Such channels are sparse in both delay and Doppler domains, enabling the transmission of the or-thogonal time frequency space (OTFS) signal efficiently expressed in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain. Thus, OTFS is regarded as a prospective modulation technique against time-varying channel. Quite a few works in OTFS only consider simple channels with integer delay in the unit of the sampling period and integer Doppler in the unit of frame frequency. For practical channel, the existing fractional delay and Doppler of the rapidly time-varying channel reduce the sparsity of the channel response and produce distinct sidelobes, leading to inter-Doppler interference (IDI) and ISI. In this paper, an improved fractional delay filter (FDF) is designed to approximate the effect of fractional delay. Based on this, an accurate signal model that reflects the impact of time-varying channel on data bits is derived. Classical zero-forcing (ZF) and minimum mean square error (MMSE) equalization algorithms are used, assuming the channel is known or estimated perfectly. Finally, instead of a simple statistical channel, we use ray-tracing (RT) to simulate the rapidly time-varying multipath channel for high-mobility scenes, with which the performance of OTFS and OFDM are simulated and compared.

articleTitle: Optimizing AoI in RIS-Aided Wireless Powered Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This study investigates in depth the expected sum age of information (AoI) in a wireless powered communication network (WPCN) incorporating reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS). In this network, a sensor harvests energy from RF signals emitted from the base station (BS) and transmits time-sensitive information to the data center. An optimization problem is formulated to minimize the expected sum AoI by jointly optimizing the phase shift of RIS and scheduling decisions. To address this problem, we develop a solution framework. Specifically, the original problem is decoupled into two sub-problems, i.e., the transmission decision problem and the phase-shift optimization problem. The transmission decision problem is analytically given a feasible solution, and the phase shift optimization problem is solved by the semi-definite relaxation (SDR) method. Simulation results demonstrate that the system's expected sum AoI is significantly enhanced by employing RIS and provide valuable insights into RIS's importance for realizing minimization AoI in WPCNs. Besides, with the increment of the generation probability, the expected sum AoI decreases.

articleTitle: MMPNet: DL-Based Low Complexity Precoding for Massive Multiuser MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Precoding is an important technology for massive multiuser multiple-input multiple-output (MU MIMO) systems to achieve high spectral efficiency. It is hard for traditional precoding algorithms to balance the high performance and computational complexity. Therefore, a low-complexity MLP-Mixer based precoding network (MMPNet) is proposed with unsupervised training, consisting of model-driven preprocessing module, data-driven feature extraction module and model-driven recovery module. The input channel information is compressed in the preprocessing module, and then converted to the key feature matrices in the feature extraction module, further the precoding matrix is calculated by the recovery module. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed MMPNet could achieve simi-lar performance to the weighted minimum mean -square error (WMMSE) algorithm with low computation complexity.

articleTitle: Fair Resource Allocation for Probabilistic Semantic Communication in IloT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of minimum rate max-imization for probabilistic semantic communication (PSCom) in industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is investigated. In the considered model, users employ semantic information extraction techniques to compress the original data before sending it to the base station (BS). During this semantic compression pro-cess, knowledge graphs are employed to represent the semantic information, and the probability graph sharing between users and the BS is utilized to further compress the knowledge graph. The semantic compression process can significantly reduce the transmitted data size, but it inevitably introduces additional computation overhead. Considering the power budget of the user, we formulate a joint communication and computation optimization problem aiming to maximize the minimum equivalent rate among all users while meeting total power and semantic compression ratio constraints. To address this problem, two algorithms with different computational complexities are proposed to obtain sub-optimal solutions. One algorithm is based on a prorate distribution of transmission power, while the other traverses the combinations of semantic compression ratios among all users. In both algorithms, bisection is employed in order to achieve the greatest minimum equivalent rate. The simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Trans-LSTMNet: An Approach of Optimization with Multi-Domain Features for CSI Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In frequency division duplexing (FDD) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, precise acquisition of downlink channel state information (CSI) through CSI feedback is crucial to harnessing the potential advantages of massive MIMO. To alleviate the excessive feedback overhead caused by the proliferation of antennas, a series of deep learning (DL)-based CSI feedback schemes have been proposed. However, most existing solutions have not fully exploited correlations among channel features of multiple domains, leading to insufficient CSI reconstruction accuracy. In this paper, a novel architecture named Trans-LSTMNet is proposed to improve the performance of CSI feedback, in which transformer is utilized to extract spatial and frequency domain features, while a memory block is designed to capture the temporal correlation based on convolutional long short-term memory (ConvLSTM). Additionally, a learnable vector quantization layer is introduced to minimize the quantization error. Results of comparable experiments show that our proposed Trans-LSTMNet could effectively improve the CSI reconstruction accuracy and significantly reduce the feedback overhead. Moreover, Trans-LSTMNet exhibits commendable generalization capability and superior performance with different settings.

articleTitle: ELM-Based CSI Feedback by Exploiting Superimposed Mode and Differential Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The channel state information (CSI) feedback in massive multiple input multiple output (mMIMO) systems demands significant user equipment (UE) energy and uplink bandwidth resources. To tackle these challenges, a novel CSI feedback is proposed, capitalizing on the benefits offered by extreme learning machine (ELM) networks, superimposed CSI feedback, and differential modulation. At the UE, subsequent to superimposed processing and symbol mapping, differential modulation is employed to reduce UE energy consumption and uplink bandwidth resource occupation. At the base station (BS), ELM networks are constructed to augment the recovery of CSI and uplink user data sequences (UL-US) by leveraging differential demodulation and symbol demapping. Simulation results demonstrate that, in comparison to pilot transmission-based CSI feedback methods, the proposed method conserves uplink bandwidth resources, diminishes UE energy consumption, and enhances the accuracy of downlink CSI reconstruction.

articleTitle: Tomlinson Harashima Precoding for Multi-User MIMO-OTFS with Reduced Overhead
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper investigates spatial domain hybrid digital-analog beamforming (BF) and Delay-Doppler (DD) domain Tomlinson-Harashima precoding (THP) for downlink mul-tiuser multiple-input and multiple-output (MU-MIMO) Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) transmission over a millimeter wave (mmWave) channel. The main challenge of this problem is that the matrix transform of the equivalent channel matrix has high complexity, which scales cubically with the product of the numbers of subcarriers, time slots, and antennas. To avoid high-complexity computation, we propose a two-step precoding scheme to cancel interference involved in the MU-MIMO-OTFS downlink transmission, with low computational complexity and signaling overhead. Our numerical results demonstrate that our proposed scheme achieves a good bit error rate (BER), which decreases linearly with transmit SNR for all users without a floor. Numerical results on the achievable sum rate are also presented, revealing that the scheme can utilize the full degree of freedom (DoF) and will not be damaged severely by the overhead.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient and Balanced Task Assignment Strategy for Multi-UAV Patrol in MEC Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper explores an inspection scenario involving multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) traversing predefined cruise points to collect data. These UAVs are connected to cellular networks and offload the collected data to ground base stations (GBSs) for processing within a restricted duration. The study proposes a balanced task allocation strategy for the patrol UAVs and an energy-efficient path design method. By jointly optimizing cruise point assignment, communication scheduling, computational resource allocation, and UAV trajectory, the approach aims to balance the completion time of multiple UAV tasks while minimizing total energy consumption. Firstly, a clustering method is introduced, which takes into account the geometric topology of cruise points, communication rate, and offload volume for task allocation. Secondly, a hybrid time-energy traveling salesman problem is formulated to determine the sequence of cruise point traversal. The energy-efficient UAV trajectory is then designed using the successive convex approximation (SCA) technique and the block coordinate descent (BCD) scheme. Numerical results indicate that the proposed balanced task allocation strategy effectively balances tasks among multiple UAVs and surpasses traditional methods in terms of task completion time and total energy consumption performance.

articleTitle: GroupMixFormer: Another Blessing of DL-Based Massive MIMO Hybrid Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The hybrid beamforming plays a critical role in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), addressing the high hardware costs associated with fully-digital beamforming. The design of hybrid beamforming, particularly satisfying the constant modulus constraint for analog beamforming, presents a complex non-convex problem. In this paper, we propose a GroupMixFormer-based hybrid beamforming network (GMF-HBN) for multi-user scenarios using orthogonal frequency di-vision multiplexing (OFDM) with both perfect and imperfect channel state information (CSI). Simulation results show a significant performance improvement of our proposed GMF-HBN with perfect CSI compared to the Transformer-based and also demonstrate robustness with imperfect CSI.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Minimization of Multi-UAV Assisted Mobile Edge Computing in SAGIN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGIN) is one of the new network architectures in the 6th Generation Mobile Communication technology (6G), which can provide higher speed and lower latency network access and coverage for ground user terminals. Under the premise of comprehensive connection, it provides solutions for service problems such as information acquisition, transmission, and processing. Given the remote geographical environment and the limited computing capability of users, SAGIN networks can provide reliable computing offload services within their coverage area by employing mobile edge computing servers on satellites and UAVs. In terms of the energy consumtion minimization problem, A Joint optimizing of offloading decision, task allocation, computing frequency and UAV deployment (JODFQ) algorithm is proposed, to decompose the original non-convex problem into three sub-problems that are iteratively solved alternately, while meeting the maximum tolerable latency of underlying tasks. Simulation results have verified the convergence and feasibility of the proposed algorithm. Compared with algorithms that use local-satellite, full-satellite and fixed UAV position schemes, the JODFQ algorithm effectively reduces the total system energy consumption. The research findings serve as a valuable reference for achieving low energy consumption and high efficiency SAGIN systems.

articleTitle: Beyond-Diagonal RIS Aided DFRC Systems: A Joint Beamforming Optimization Design Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) acts as a new RIS paradigm to increase the design degrees of freedom as well as enlarge serving coverage areas. To explore the benefits of BD-RIS for both sensing and communication in the future communication networks, we investigate a BD-RIS assisted dual-function radar-communication (DFRC) system for beamforming design, where the weighted sum-rate (WSR) of users is maximized by jointly designing the transmit precoder and the BD-RIS matrices under different RIS architectures. To tackle the non-convex problem, we propose an alternating optimization approach based on the weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) framework, fractional programming, and manifold optimization. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach and the superiority of employing BD-RIS in DFRC systems to enhance both communication and radar performance.

articleTitle: Active-RIS-Aided Covert Communications in NOMA-Inspired ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-inspired integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) facilitates spectrum sharing for radar sensing and NOMA communications, whereas facing privacy and security challenges due to open wireless propagation. In this paper, active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is employed to aid covert communications in NOMA-inspired ISAC wireless system with the aim of maximizing the covert rate. Specifically, a dual-function base-station (BS) transmits the superposition signal to sense multiple targets, while achieving covert and reliable communications for a pair of NOMA covert and public users, respectively, in the presence of a warden. To maximize the covert rate, the transmission beamforming at BS and reflection beamforming at active-RIS are jointly designed, subject to quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of NOMA public user, constraint of Cramér-Rao bound for multi-target estimations, and covertness level against warden. To this end, we develop the efficient methods involving the penalized Dinkelbach transformation to convert the non-concave covert rate maximization problem into the feasible one and propose an alternating optimization algorithm to obtain stationary solutions for the original problem. Numerical results demonstrate that active-RIS-aided NOMA-ISAC system outperforms the passive-RIS-aided and without- RIS counterparts in terms of covert rate and trade-off between covert communication and sensing performance metrics.

articleTitle: Satellite Coverage Traffic Deviation Prediction for LEO Constellation Networks Based on CNN-LSTM Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Satellite traffic experiences significant fluctuations due to factors such as satellite dynamics, user distribution, and Earth rotation, causing uneven satellite traffic distribution for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellation networks. In this paper, to predict the coverage traffic, a prediction method of Satellite Coverage Traffic Volume Deviation (SCTVD) based on the Spatiotemporal model (SCTVD-ST) for the LEO constellation networks traffic prediction problem is proposed. This method integrates satellite dynamics to map satellite positional information to traffic. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are employed to extract spatial and temporal features from traffic volume deviation, respectively. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and stability of the proposed SCTVD-ST model and demonstrate that predicting traffic deviations and then correcting traffic outperform predicting traffic directly.

articleTitle: Federated-TD3:Joint Computing Offloading and Resource Allocation in Urban Air Mobility
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With rapid urban population growth and urban-ization, along with increasing demand for developing the low- altitude economy, urban air mobility (UAM) is seen as a way to alleviate ground traffic congestion and promote the low-altitude economy. Due to frequent data computation, low latency require-ments, and limited energy, effective computation offloading and resource management are urgently needed. This paper assumes UAM aircraft transmit semantic information and proposes a computation offloading and resource allocation strategy based on edge computing (EC). In case of edge server failure, relay UAV s assist in information transmission, enabling UAM aircraft to offload tasks to other edge servers. We formulated an op-timization problem to minimize delay and energy consumption and designed the Federated- Td3algorithm, combining federated learning (FL) and twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3). Compared to two baseline algorithms, our algorithm reduced delay by 9.9% and 3.3%, and energy consumption by 14.1 % and 4.5%.

articleTitle: Physical Intrusion Detection via Signal Reflection in Fieldbus Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: As the underlying network of wind energy con-version systems (WECS), fieldbus networks are typically pro-tected from cyber attacks through network isolation. However, attackers can bypass the isolation mechanism and physically connect malicious devices to networks to launch various attacks. Existing methods mainly focus on obtaining abnormal signals from intrusion devices to detect intrusion devices. However, these methods cannot detect inactive intrusion devices which only eavesdrop without sending any signals. In this paper, we discover signal differences caused by reflection signals and propose a physical intrusion detection method based on reflection signal extraction. By extracting the voltage characteristics of the rising and falling edges of normal transmission signals and constructing fingerprints, our method can effectively detect inactive intrusion devices. The experimental results on a real CAN testbed show that the F -score for detecting inactive intrusion devices can reach 95.2 % in various attack scenarios.

articleTitle: Deployment Optimization of Multi-Cell Multi-User System with Hard Core Poisson Point Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the continuous development of information and communication technology, the scale of communication systems and the randomness of wireless signals increase. Hence it is urgent to analyze the coverage performance of communication system with a realistic signal model. In this paper, considering the Hard Core Point Process (HCPP) in stochastic geometry, the multi-cell system is modeled. Moreover, we obtain the closed-form expression of the system coverage probability. In particular, a system deployment expense function is proposed, which is related to the density of base stations, power consumption and outage probability. The optimization algorithm is exploited, and the optimal base station density and minimum system deployment expense are obtained. It is proved by simulation that the system deployment strategy in this paper can effectively optimize the deployment of the base stations system.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Network Slicing Resource Allocation for ISAC Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: A hierarchical network slicing resource scheduling architecture is proposed for multiple types of vehicle services under the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) cell-free network. Considering the quality of the slicing service and the fairness of vehicle user equipment, an optimization problem to maximize the long-term system effectiveness is proposed for the transmission model of both sensing slicing and communication slicing services. The convergence strategy of the associated configuration of power scheduling and resource blocks (RB) is solved by continuous convex approximation and alternate iteration optimization in the transmission time interval layer control strategy. In the time frame layer control strategy, the number of RB slices is allocated by the double-deep Q network algorithm. The simulation results show the superiority of the proposed hierarchical scheduling scheme, which can satisfy the latency and reliability performance of different types of services.

articleTitle: Co-Frequency Signal Separation Technique in IRS Channel Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In order to address the issue of mixed signal in an Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted wireless communication system, FastICA blind source separation (BSS) algorithm with wavelet threshold denoising is proposed. The observed signal is denoised by wavelet threshold to filter the noise in wireless communication environment, and then use FastICA algorithm based on maximum negative entropy to process the mixed signal after denoising, and realize the separation and extraction of legitimate signal and interference signal. Simulation results show that this algorithm enhances the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) in the communication system and successfully isolates same frequency mixed signals.

articleTitle: Hybrid ToA and Fingerprinting Localization Enabled by Channel Knowledge Map
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Time-of-arrival (ToA) and fingerprinting are two classical approaches for indoor localization. With line-of-sight (LoS) links, the ToA information can be used to correctly estimate the range between the transmitter and the target. However, the accuracy of ToA localization degrades drastically if some LoS links are blocked. On the other hand, fingerprinting localization relies on the variation of signal features at different locations, which makes it suitable for rich scattering environment. However, due to the environment dynamics and measurement noise, fingerprinting can hardly achieve high localization accuracy, especially if only sparse and simple fingerprints are available, e.g., the received signal strength (RSS). To benefit from both approaches, the paper proposes a hybrid ToA and fingerprinting localization enabled by the channel knowledge map (CKM). Specifically, we construct a channel gain map (CGM) based on sampled RSS measurements, which is used as the fingerprints for coarse localization. Besides, the link state map (LSM) is also constructed based on the prior physical environment information and the CGM, which stores the LoS link status at various locations within the area of interest. Given the coarse target location, those transmitters that have LoS links with the target are identified based on the LSM, and then ToA information from those transmitters is used to refine the localization. Simulation results show that the proposed hybrid localization scheme can significantly outperform that benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Wi-Fi Beyond Communications: Experimental Evaluation of Respiration Monitoring and Motion Detection Using COTS Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Wi-Fi sensing has become an attractive option for non-invasive monitoring of human activities and vital signs. This paper explores the feasibility of using state-of-the-art commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) devices for Wi-Fi sensing applications, particularly respiration monitoring and motion detection. We utilize the Intel AX210 network interface card (NIC) to transmit Wi-Fi signals in both 2.4 GHz and 6 GHz frequency bands. Our experiments rely on channel frequency response (CFR) and received signal strength indicator (RSSI) data, which are processed using a moving average algorithm to extract human behavior patterns. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in capturing and representing human respiration and motion patterns. Furthermore, we compare the performance of Wi-Fi sensing across different frequency bands, highlighting the advantages of using higher frequencies for improved sensitivity and clarity. Our findings showcase the practicality of using COTS devices for Wi-Fi sensing and lay the groundwork for the development of non-invasive, contactless sensing systems. These systems have potential applications in various fields, including healthcare, smart homes, and Metaverse.

articleTitle: Robust Transceiver Beamforming for Multi-user ISAC System with Direction Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we study robust transmit precoding and receive beamforming design for a multiple user terminals (UTs) integrated sensing and communication system with targets and clutters direction uncertainty. Then, we formulate the worst-case robust optimization problem by maximizing the minimal signal-to-clutter plus interference and noise ratio (SCINR) among all UTs with the constraints of UT transmit power budget and minimum communication rate. Moreover, using the generalized Rayleigh quotient and SCINR lower bound, we tackle the sensing SCINR constraint. Then, we adopt the quadratic transform based Lagrangian dual transform to deal with the communication rate constraint. Finally, we propose an iterative optimization algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in improving the performance of ISAC system.

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Downlink Resource Allocation in Beam Hopping LEO Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Beam hopping (BH) technology has become a criti-cal satellite beam scheduling technique due to its high resource utilization and flexibility. To improve resource utilization in low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication systems, the objective of this paper is to maximize energy efficiency (EE) under the constraint of minimum offered capacity to demand ratio (OCDR) by scheduling multi-time-slot beams and allocating power among beams. The multi-time-slot problem is first transformed into a single time-slot problem and further decomposed into power allocation and user selection sub-problems. Then, an iterative algorithm is designed to solve the power allocation problem, and an energy efficient user selection algorithm is proposed based on the power allocation results and the user priority. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm could satisfy the minimum OCDR requirements and meanwhile significantly improves the system EE.

articleTitle: Will Element Grouping Enhance Covert Communication Performance in ARIS-Aided NOMA Systems?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper investigates the impacts of element grouping on the covert communication performance of an active reconfigurable intelligent surface (ARIS)-aided non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system. Through element grouping, each element of the ARIS works in either the reflecting mode to reflect the information signal or the jamming mode to generate jamming signal. Optimizing the NOMA transmit power, jamming power, ARIS beamforming, and receive beamforming jointly is necessary to maximize the covert communication rate. To tackle the unsolvable covert communication rate maximization problem, we decouple the original problem into four sub-problems of optimizing NOMA transmit power, jamming power, ARIS beamforming, and receive beamforming, respectively. To tackle the mixed-integer non-linear programming for element grouping, we introduce the arithmetic and geometric mean-based penalty term and apply the Dinkelbach transform to reformulate the optimization problem. Next, we propose an alternating optimization algorithm to optimize the system parameters. The numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the element grouping in improving the covert communication rate. However, the element grouping scheme achieves a lower covert communication rate performance compared to the scheme without element grouping, indicating that using element grouping for covert communications in the ARIS-aided NOMA system is not the preferred option.

articleTitle: CKMImageNet: A Comprehensive Dataset to Enable Channel Knowledge Map Construction via Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Environment-aware communication and sensing is one of the promising paradigm shifts towards 6G, which fully leverages prior information of the local wireless environment to optimize network performance. One of the key enablers for environment-aware communication and sensing is channel knowledge map (CKM), which provides location-specific channel knowledge that is crucial for channel state information (CSI) acquisition. To support the efficient construction of CKM, large-scale location-specific channel data is essential. However, most existing channel datasets do not have the location information nor visual representations of channel data, making them inadequate for exploring the intrinsic relationship between the channel knowledge and the local environment, nor for applying advanced artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms such as computer vision (CV) for CKM construction. To address such issues, in this paper, a large-scale dataset named CKMImageNet is established, which can provide both location-tagged numerical channel data and visual images, providing a holistic view of the channel and environment. Built using commercial ray tracing software, CKMImageNet captures electromagnetic wave propagation in different scenarios, revealing the relationships between location, environment and channel knowledge. By integrating detailed channel data and the corresponding image, CKMImageNet not only supports the verification of various communication and sensing algorithms, but also enables CKM construction with CV algorithms.

articleTitle: Hybrid Demodulation: A Optimal Demodulation Scheme for MU-MIMO-ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) plays a crucial role in the 6G era by combining sensing and communication functions. The use of a superposition waveform, where the sensing signal is integrated with the communication signal, is an effective strategy for utilizing the same resources. Current approaches using uniform demodulation methods for all users like direct and successive interference cancelation (SIC) may not perform optimally in MIMO-ISAC systems. In MIMO systems, communication users in different directions may experience different levels of interference from the sensing signal. Therefore, a more refined approach involves using specific demodulation schemes tailored to users facing different sensing interferences. This study proposes a hybrid demodulation scheme for communication users of the MIMO-ISAC systems, which adopt diverse demodulation approaches for multiple users by joint power allocation strategy. The selection of demodulation schemes, such as direct or SIC demodulation, is based on the prevailing sensing interference on the communication signal. The proposed design improves the bit error rate of communication users and reduces the distortion of the sensing beampattern induced by the communication signal. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed waveform design.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Assisted User Tracking with Sliding Window in Space-Confined Tunnels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In recent years, reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted localization has garnered significant attention. However, there has been relatively limited research on RIS assisted user tracking, especially in space-confined tunnels. To this end, this paper proposes a novel RIS-assisted user tracking scheme. In this scheme, we first segment a strip-shaped RIS to address the near-field approximation in constrained tunnel environments.
