Then, we combine a sliding-window RIS with an extended Kalman filter (EKF) for user tracking, where the sliding-window RIS ensures that the user remains within the tracking beam, and the EKF achieves real-time tracking. Finally, numerical results show that the proposed approach achieves effective user mobility tracking and outperforms the traditional tracking scheme in space-confined tunnels.

articleTitle: Delay-Aware Parallel Offloading AIGC Service in Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Mobile edge computing (MEC) enabled artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) has garnered significant attention. To support AIGC metaverse applications within MEC, it is effective to offload computation tasks, particularly those involving neural networks AIGC, from mobile devices to edge clouds. Existing solutions typically assume the availability of a dedicated and powerful edge server for each user, which can handle the entire AIGC service offloading. However, in practical scenarios, the availability of such dedicated and powerful servers may be limited, necessitating the utilization of less capable alternatives. Thus, we propose the delay-aware parallel offloading AIGC framework which partitions multi-modal content and offloads partial diffusion tasks to multiple servers. The proposed scheme accelerates mobile deep vision multi-modal metaverse applications by leveraging parallel offloading for any server provisioning. Our framework integrates recurrent region proposal prediction algorithm with delay-aware multi-modal parallel diffusion offloading scheme, optimizing communication and computing resources while minimizing delay in wireless environments. Simulation results show that our approach can reduce delay by 20% compared to conventional algorithms.

articleTitle: Matching Game-Based Heterogeneous Network Selection for UAVs in Underground Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are a novel type of device for daily monitoring due to their mobility and modular application. In this paper, a network selection algorithm with on-demand dynamic matching is proposed to ensure stable access to heterogeneous networks in underground spaces for UAV s. Specifically, considering the mobility of UAV s and the complex propagation characteristics in underground spaces, we construct a multi-objective combinatorial optimization problem for hetero-geneous network selection based on the preferences of different types of services for communication indicators. To solve the combinatorial optimization problem, we first design a weighted algorithm based on the intuitionistic fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (IFAHP) to transform the multi-objective optimization problem into a single-objective one. Then, we propose a matching game-based algorithm to improve the satisfaction of UAV s with the network. The simulation results show that our algorithm can achieve a balanced optimization of the transmission rate, delay, and hand off cost of UAV s in underground spaces.

articleTitle: Joint User and Target Tracking in Multi-Static Sensing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Perceiving the mobility of the passive targets is critical in the context of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC). While target localization has been extensively studied in radio sensing, the motion estimation and tracking of the targets have not been revealed. This paper proposes a new framework for joint UE and target tracking in the multi-static sensing system under the promising scenario that the user equipment (UE) serves as the receiver. We first estimate the UE's location using the direct paths between the UE and the base stations (BSs), and estimate the target's location of each scattering path to identify the targets by the mean-shift clustering algorithm. Then, we jointly estimate the motions of the UE and targets using the Taylor-least squares (LS) algorithm, and propose a joint UE and target tracking method based on the extended Kalman filter (EKF). Simulations demonstrate that the proposed joint motion estimation and tracking scheme improves the accuracy of location estimates by 42.34% w.r.t. the UE, and 71.29% w.r.t. the targets.

Author Keywords: joint user equipment (UE) and target tracking

articleTitle: Multi-Device Cooperative Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models at the Network Edge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The emergence of large-scale foundation models (FoMo's) that can perform human-like intelligence inspires edge devices to access state-of-the-art artificial intelligence (AI) applications. For a better user experience, the pre-trained FoMo needs to be adapted for specialized downstream tasks through fine-tuning techniques. To transcend a single device's memory and computation limitations, we propose a multi-device cooperation mechanism within the device-edge cooperative fine-tuning (DEFT) paradigm, where devices distributed at the wireless edge simultaneously optimize different parts of fine-tuning parameters within a FoMo. The edge server is responsible for coordination and update aggregation. However, the parameter blocks resided in different depths within a FoMo architecture, leading to varied computation latency and memory consumption due to the adoption of gradient backpropagation-based calculations. The hetero-geneous on-device computation capability and memory budget, block calculation latency, and uploading channel conditions, necessitate an integrated communication-and-computation (C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) allocation of local computation loads and uplink communication resources to achieve low-latency DEFT (LoLa-DEFT). To address this issue, a depth-aware block allocation problem is formulated and solved optimally, which aims to pick up the device-block pairs with the best C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> performance while satisfying related constraints. Through extensive experiments conducted on the GLUE benchmark, our results demonstrate the proposed depth-aware block allocation for LoLa DEFT achieves a substantial acceleration in fine-tuning a RoBERTa model compared with traditional computation offloading scheme.

articleTitle: Cross-Slot User Scheduling Strategy for Fast Uplink Grant over Cell-Free Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Fast uplink grant effectively copes with massive ultra-reliable and low-latency communication (mURLLC) by virtue of collision avoidance and overhead savings. However, its access performance is limited by active prediction and user scheduling, resulting in serious resource wastage and accumulation of failed users. To solve this problem, we propose a cross-slot user scheduling strategy based on cell-free architecture. The strategy designs the post-compensation stage and pre-experience stage in the fast uplink grant mechanism, in which the prediction error is compensated by reserving resources to provide random access to active users, while the generated access information obtained is combined with the prediction information of the new active users as the priori information to improve one-time access success probability in continous access slots. Simulation results show that the cross-slot user scheduling strategy can effectively compensate the prediction error, greatly avoid the backlog of failed users, and reduce the access delay.

articleTitle: Intelligent Active Handover Decision Algorithm for Uplink Transmission of Delay-Sensitive Tasks in LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the sharp growth of user service demand and the rapid development of satellite payload and communication technology, the utility of low earth orbit (LEO) satellite network in the 6th generation (6G) has become a promising trend. However, due to the high mobility of LEO satellites and the overlapping terrestrial coverage, traditional handover decision methods are difficult to meet the requirements of low delay and low overhead. Therefore, in this paper, we consider a scenario in which a terrestrial user transmits delay-sensitive task to LEO satellite networks to study the handover decision during the uplink process. First, we model the handover decision problem as an integer programming problem. To solve the above formulated problem, we propose a multi-round replay proximal policy optimization (MrRPPO) algorithm. By reasonably increasing the number of rounds in the online replay buffers, the agent improves the searching ability and can achieve faster convergence and better results. Comprehensive simulations illustrate that the proposed method is able to minimize the total uplink delay, with as low handover times as possible, compared to other benchmark algorithms.

articleTitle: Detection Probability and Rate Tradeoff in MIMO-OFDM ISAC System With Imperfect Channel Information
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper investigates the probability of detection (PD) and rate tradeoff for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) based on multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) orthog-onal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) framework with multi-beam. In particular, we consider a superposition model where sensing signal and communication signal occupy non-overlapping OFDM sub carriers. Sensing signal is used as pilots such that the detection is carried out over channel estimations. We derive the theoretical expression for PD and consider the performance tradeoff against average capacity lower bound. The performance tradeoff between sensing and communication system as influenced by beamforming and subcarrier power allocation is then characterized and contextualized through simulations.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Adaptive OFDM MIMO Equalization in Intelligence-Native RAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into 6G radio access network (RAN) architectures is essential for advancing communication technologies. This paper introduces a novel approach for orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) equalization using Transformer networks to perform in-context learning (ICL) under unknown channel conditions. By leveraging received-transmitted pilot symbol pairs, the proposed method enables the Transformer to infer equalized signals efficiently, dynamically adapting to varying sub channel allocations and frequency-selective channels. This approach enhances spectral efficiency, mitigates interference, and ensures robust signal equalization within intelligence-native RANs. The flexibility of our model aligns with fully decoupled RAN architectures, demonstrating significant improvements in user service delivery and physical laver transmission.

articleTitle: Joint Data Sampling and Client Scheduling for Over-the-Air Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Wireless federated learning (FL) can effectively exploit the rich data distributed at edge devices for network edge intelligence. However, the contradictions between the huge training data and the limited computing capability of devices, as well as between the massive sharing model parameters and the limited communication resources, severely limit the performance of FL at the edge. To overcome these challenges, this paper adopts analog over-the-air computation and jointly considers training sample selection, model pruning, and client scheduling for FL. We first derive an upper bound for the accuracy loss of the aggregation model, considering communication error, model pruning loss, sample selection, and model training cumulative error. A joint problem is formulated based on computation-communication cost and model accuracy loss to balance the training cost and model quality. Then we propose a joint optimization of computation and communication resources algorithm to minimize the objective function. Simulation results demonstrate that this algorithm significantly reduces the overall cost of model aggregation while ensuring model accuracy.

articleTitle: UAV-Based Coverage Hole Detection and Recovery For Large-Scale IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Large-scale Internet of Things (IoT) networks are widely deployed in applications such as the Internet of Vehicles, thanks to their agile and reliable Internet connectivity. Typically, data collected by various IoT devices is aggregated and routed by a gateway in long-range wide-area networks (LPWANs) or a base station (BS) in legacy cellular networks to a remote cloud platform for data analysis and statistics. The extensive use of IoT applications has led to rapid network densification, posing a new challenge for sixth-generation (6G) systems regarding coverage planning. Conventional techniques for detecting coverage holes on the ground, such as the minimization of drive tests, are severely limited by high costs and time consumption. To address these challenges, we propose using a patrol UAV to identify coverage holes within a specified area. Once identified, an individual UAV or a swarm of UAVs can be deployed as an aerial BS, either scheduled by a satellite or a nearby terrestrial BS, to restore service quality on demand. The UAV swarm is organized based on Delaunay triangulation, which can be expanded to accommodate more enormous swarms while allowing for analytical mathematical analysis based on stochastic geometry theory. Simulation results corroborate the cost-effectiveness and time efficiency of this proposed approach in identifying coverage holes and providing on-demand recovery.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Distributed Queueing Based Grant-Free Random Access Protocol for Satellite Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Satellite-based Internet of Things (IoT), as an augment and extension of the terrestrial IoT, is expected to achieve the true interconnection of everything in the sixth-generation vision. However, in view of the massive and concurrent access requests within wide area coverage and the limited spectrum re-sources, the realization of efficient random access (RA) contention resolution has become one of the major bottlenecks constraining the performance of satellite-IoT systems. In this paper, we propose an adaptive distributed queuing (ADQ) mechanism based grant-free RA protocol to enhance access efficiency and resource utilization in massive bursty access scenarios. Particularly, the proposed protocol optimizes the consolidation of subgroups with low preamble resource occupancy during the later contention resolution stages, which can significantly enhance the overall access timeliness while ensuring high access success rates of devices. In addition, we develop a mathematical analysis model for the proposed protocol to accurately estimate its blocking prob-ability, average access delay, and average energy consumption. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of theoretical analysis and demonstrate that, in the case of 1500 concurrent access devices, the average access delay and average energy consumption of our protocol are reduced by 41 % and 17 % respectively, as compared with the conventional DQ-based RA protocol, while maintaining a extremely low blocking probability.

articleTitle: Backdoor Detection in Digital Twin-Driven Smart Grid via Contribution Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the integration of smart grid and digital twin technologies, federated learning becomes pivotal in ensuring privacy-preserving AI model training. In such scenarios, each user within the smart grid is geographically dispersed, prohibiting the sharing of raw data to safeguard privacy. However, this setup is susceptible to backdoor attacks. When an attacker initiates such an attack, the smart grid model is manipulated to produce the attacker's desired output, while maintaining normal functionality under standard conditions. The inherent distributed nature of federated learning complicates the detection of backdoor attacks. To address this, we model the federated learning process within a digital twin as a cooperative game. By employing the Shapley value to measure the contribution of nodes in each training round, we propose an outlier detection algorithm to identify malicious users. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm has been evaluated via extensive experiments.

articleTitle: Channel Knowledge Map-Enhanced Clutter Suppression for Integrated Sensing and Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Clutter suppression has been an essential problem for radar sensing, while traditional techniques such as moving target indication (MTI) and pulse Doppler (PD) usually give poor performance for slow and small targets. In this paper, motivated by the concept of channel knowledge map (CKM), we propose a novel clutter suppression technique for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems by leveraging a new type of CKM named clutter angle map (CLAM). CLAM is a site-specific database, containing the primary clutter angles for each location of interest. With such pre-acquired clutter angle information, the sensing signal components corresponding to the clutter environment can be removed before target detection and parameter estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed CLAM-based technique effectively suppresses clutter and enhances target sensing performance, achieving higher esti-mation accuracy for sensing slow and small targets.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Non-Binary Polar Codes for Compressing Mitochondrial Genomes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In response to the compression and storage challenges of genomic sequencing data, this paper proposes a method called DeepPolarMitoComp (DPMC), which combines an attention-based convolutional neural network (CNN) with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network and q-ary polar codes for compressing mitochondrial genomes. The CNN is employed to identify local features and patterns within the genome sequences, while the LSTM captures the temporal correlations and long-term dependencies to identify global features. The attention mechanism is integrated to enhance the capacity of model and the prediction performance by focusing on important base positions. Additionally, polar codes, as a novel coding scheme and a candidate coding technique in 3GPP standards, are utilized for source coding. The neural network prediction model outputs the probability distribution of the next base in the genomic sequence, and polar codes are applied for entropy coding. Experimental results on complete mitochondrial genome datasets of Homo sapiens demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. The code for DPMC is available at the following GitHub repository: https://github.com/JinWang00/DPMC.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Collaborative Defense Strategies Against Malicious Traffic in Wireless Edge Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack is a kind of critical threat for wireless edge network that flood networks with malicious traffic, which is difficult to defense due to the traffic fluctuation. To efficiently detect and countermeasure the DDoS attack, we propose a multi-level collaborative defense strategy that facilitates lightweight and cost-effective malicious traffic detection. The interaction between attacker and defender is modeled as a two-stage Stackelberg game and the optimal defense strategy is obtained with equilibrium analysis. We utilize the gradient descent method to iteratively compute the optimal strategies for both the attacker and the defender. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy can significantly enhance the utility of the defender, while reducing the utility of the attacker. In addition, when the attacker has access to a consider-able number of nodes, our approach demonstrably outperforms existing schemes.

articleTitle: Intelligent Congestion Control in QUIC for Reliable E2E Communication Network: A Digital Twin-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a digital twin-based intelligent congestion control approach to enhance the packet transmission adaptability and efficiency of the QUIC protocol within dynamic network environments. Specifically, by integrating actor-critic learning methods, the proposed approach adaptively tailors the pre-defined congestion control parameter settings to suit various application scenarios, thereby optimizing QUIC's performance under fluctuating network conditions. In addition, utilizing digital twin technology, the algorithm constructs a simulation model that mirrors the physical network within a digital framework. This model facilitates the rapid collection of network data, precise monitoring of congestion levels, and detailed analysis of historical transmission records and network state changes. These capabilities enable the predictive adjustment of model parameters and timely modifications to the congestion control strategy, ensuring optimal performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed digital twin-based intelligent approach can enhance QUIC's transmission capabilities across diverse network conditions. Notably, it increases data throughput, reduces transmission delays, improves the convergence speed of the intelligence algorithm, and ensures reliable end-to-end transmissions within 5G networks.

articleTitle: Robust Beamforming Design for Intelligent Reflecting Surface Assisted ISAC Systems with Imperfect CSI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper investigates the robust beamforming design of intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) assisted integrated sensing and communication systems (ISAC) with imperfect channel state information (CSI). By maximizing the beampattern gain towards the target given the average mean squared error (MSE) requirement, the performance of communication and sensing can be guaranteed. Our objective is to optimize the transmit/receive beamformers and IRS phase shifts simultaneously to maximize the beampattern gain towards the target. In particular, an effective algorithm is proposed to solve the non-convex optimization problem by using majorization-minimization (MM) techniques as well as semi-definite relaxation (SDR) techniques. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of our proposed scheme in achieving a robust beampattern gain performance in the presence of CSI estimation errors, which outperforms conventional non-robust methods.

articleTitle: DT-GCN Based Digital Twin for 6G Self-Intelligent Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the rapid development of Sixth Generation (6G) self-intelligent network, higher requirements are put forward for intelligent decision, high-precision configuration, self-learning and self-optimization of the network. Digital twin, as digital representation of physical network, can enhance the capabilities of physical network in terms of data perception, intelligent decision-making, and pre-validation to enable the realization of closed-loop autonomy in 6G network. However, the precise and efficient construction of digital twin network (DTN) faces challenges due to the complexity of network, which in turn can affect the accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI) based intelligent policies pre-validation. Therefore, a data-driven Digital Twin architecture for 6G self-intelligent network is proposed in this paper. Based on this architecture, the method of digital representation based on Graph Sample and Aggregation (GraphSAGE) towards global network is innovatively proposed, aiming at mining and extracting the deep correlation of network nodes in global topology information. Moreover, a digital twin graph convolutional network (DT-GCN) which taking representation of digital twin as prior knowledge, is constructed for network decision-making pre-validation, and this provides more precision for intelligent policy. Finally, the DT-GCN is introduced to realize the application of network fault pre-validation with greater accuracy and speed. The results show that DT -GCN improves policies accuracy by 4.98% and convergence speed by 7.14% compared to traditional GCN method.

articleTitle: Mask Learning Enabled Multi-Task Semantic Communication with Adaptive Rate Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Semantic communication, a novel paradigm in communication, could significantly enhance communication efficiency by extracting and transmitting semantic information relevant to artificial intelligence (AI) tasks. In practice, a device may need to perform multiple AI tasks, and the semantic features required for each task are usually different. If multiple tasks share a single encoder to extract generalized semantic features, there is unnec-essary communication overhead. To solve the above issue, this paper introduces a mask learning enabled multi-task semantic communication system with adaptive rate control (ARC-MTSC) to extract and transmit customized semantic features according to different tasks. First, a lightweight feature selection network (FSN) is proposed, which can change the number of features depending on variable channel conditions and choose desired features for each task. Then, to achieve adaptive rate control, the FSN generates a mask vector to dynamically adjust the number of transmitted features, allowing the system to adaptively balance transmission rate and task performance. The results of the simulation demonstrate that the ARC-MTSC greatly decreases transmission overhead while maintaining negligible performance loss compared to the single-task baseline.

articleTitle: Joint Compression Ratio and User Association for Multi-Cell Probabilistic Semantic Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, the sum rate maximization problem for a multi-cell downlink probalistic semantic communication (PSCom) system is investigated. In the considered model, each base station (BS) employs semantic information extraction techniques to compress raw data before transmitting it to the user. At the receiving side, the user recovers the compressed information through a knowledge base shared with the served BS. Our model encapsulates large data within a comprehensive knowledge graph and leverages a shared probabilistic graph between users and BSs for efficient semantic compression. Taking into account the total power budget, semantic resource limitation constraints, and user association parameters, the sum semantic rate maximization problem is formulated through jointly optimizing the semantic compression ratio, transmit power, and user association. This joint optimization problem balances transmission efficiency and computational complexity. To tackle this optimization problem, an iterative algorithm is proposed where the optimal solution for a specific user's semantic compression ratio is determined in each iteration. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

articleTitle: Secure OTFS Transmission via Joint Delay-Doppler Precoding and Time-Domain Noise Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: This paper studied the secure transmission problem for a single-antenna orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) system where a transmitter sends private information to legitimate receiver with the existence of a potential eavesdropper. Without multiple antennas, we propose a joint delay-Doppler (DD) domain and time domain secure transmission strategy, instead of the traditional ones based on multi-antenna precoding. The DD-domain precoding matrix and time-domain artificial noise (AN) vector are jointly optimized to maximize the system secrecy rate. The cases where eavesdropper's channel state information (CSI) is available and unavailable are both investigated. Moreover, a low-complexity projected gradient (PG)-based algorithm is developed. Numerical results show that the benefit of time-domain AN in terms of secrecy rate becomes more significant as the total available transmit power increases. In addition, the low-complexity PG algorithm can significantly reduce computational complexity with only negligible secrecy rate loss.

articleTitle: Digital Wireless Semantic Communication Enabled by the Discrete Semantic Knowledge Base and Updating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Semantic Knowledge Base (SKB) based on semantic communication attracts increasing attention, since SKB can provide shared knowledge to codecs and improve communication efficiency. However, it has become one of the major challenges for efficient semantic knowledge base communication systems to combat channel noise when facing varying data sources. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a Digital Semantic Communication Enabled by the Discrete Semantic Knowledge Base and Updating (DSC-DSKB) for overcoming channel noise and enhancing communication robustness. Specifically, this paper defines a discrete codebook as a Discrete Semantic Knowledge Base (DSKB) and introduces digital quantization in the Communication process to build the DSC-DSKB. When the DSKB distribution type of the receiver and the transmitter differ, the receiver should update the DSKB to make up the performance gap. Therefore, we propose an update strategy for DSKB, which updates the knowledge base data through the index knowledge heatmap. The experimental results demonstrate that the DSC-DSKB significantly enhances communication performance while keeping the same channel bandwidth as the traditional approach. Meanwhile, the update approach for DSKB effectively maintains high performance while reducing the amount of data delivered.

articleTitle: Joint Power Allocation and Reliability Optimization with Generative AI for Wireless Networked Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Leveraging the characteristics of wireless connectivity, wireless networked control systems (WNCSs) offer high flexibility and low deployment costs, garnering widespread interest. However, the time-varying nature of wireless channels poses significant challenges to the control reliability of WNCS. To meet the stringent control reliability and rate performance demands in factory automation scenarios, we propose a novel joint optimization design for the uplink transmission of sensors in multi-loop WNCSs. Our goal is to maximize the sum rate by jointly optimizing power allocation at the base station and reliability at the control systems (CSs), while considering practical constraints such as packet error rate (PER), control stability, and energy. We derive an expression for the PER and system state convergence to guide the co-design process, and then introduce a generative AI-based joint power and reliability optimization strategy. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms several baseline algorithms, significantly enhancing the sum rate performance while ensuring system control stability.

articleTitle: Fair Communication Resource Scheduling in 6G and Digital Twin-Driven Virtual Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: A virtual power plant (VPP) is a technology and management system that integrates distributed energy resources, offering significant advantages for the access and management of these distributed energy resources. With the development of distributed energy, higher requirements are being placed on the communication resource scheduling capabilities of virtual power plants. For dense source-load-storage devices, the high bandwidth, low latency, and high energy efficiency characteristics of 6G networks can meet the control requirements of virtual power plants for these devices. Digital twins are currently widely used in the industrial sector, providing positive effects such as real-time monitoring, prediction, and performance optimization. Applying digital twins to the communication resource scheduling of virtual power plants enables real-time perception of resource allocation and timely resource scheduling. This paper proposes a communication resource scheduling algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning, leveraging digital twin technology and the 6G distributed subnet architecture. This algorithm aims to efficiently utilize limited resources such as resource blocks, spectrum, and power to balance system throughput, fairness, and scheduling latency, thereby ensuring the QoS of source-load-storage device scheduling tasks. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed resource scheduling algorithm enhances system throughput and fairness while meeting scheduling latency requirements, thereby satisfying the QoS needs of scheduling tasks.

articleTitle: Diversity Analysis of MIMO-OTFS in Multipath Rapid Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Key research has demonstrated that orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation can naturally achieve a maximum diversity gain equal to the number of propagation paths in time-variant channels, under the assumption of quasi-static conditions where channel coefficients remain constant in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain per frame. However, in scenarios where the channel undergoes rapid fading, this assumption may no longer hold. It is noteworthy that although rapid fading alters the input-output relation of OTFS, such channels can provide extra degrees of freedom (DoFs) that can be utilized by OTFS, as confirmed by recent studies. This paper further investigates the impact of available DoFs in the joint spatial and DD domains on error performance. We derive the pairwise error probability (PEP) of MIMO-OTFS and illustrate its achievable maximum and asymptotic diversity gains, which are demonstrated using the inherent diversity distribution properties of OTFS modulation. Additionally, we validate the effect of path correlation on system performance. Simulation results confirm the aforementioned theoretical conclusions.

articleTitle: Fast Content Delievery Based on Optimization of Multi-layer Cache-enabled UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: With the wide use of mobile applications, the amount of data and content in networks increases explosively, bringing severe challenges to content delivery in traditional cellular networks. This paper proposes a multi-layer UAV proactive caching model to minimize content delivery delay. Specifically, flexible but limited-capacity quadrotor UAVs serve as low-altitude platforms (LAPs) to provide content for clustered users. The airship is deployed as a high-altitude platform (HAP) to cover all users and overcome the limited caching of the LAPs. The joint optimization of inter-layer content caching and LAPs' three-dimensional (3-D) deployment is a mixed-integer optimization problem, which is challenging to solve. We decompose the original problem into a knapsack problem and a LAPs' 3-D deployment problem. The non-deterministic polynomial hard (NP-hard) knapsack problem is solved by proposing content popularity-first (CPF) and content diversity-first (CDF) caching strategies. The LAPs' 3-D deployment problem is broken down into quasiconvex vertical and convex horizontal optimization problems to be solved separately. Experimental results show that proactive caching by exploiting multi-layer UAVs can reduce transmission delay.

articleTitle: Achieving Improved Security in UAV-Assisted Covert Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Covert communication can hide confidential signals in environmental noise to avoid being detected and provide comprehensive security for wireless transmission. However, there still exists significant risks in the wireless transmission once being detected. In this paper, we propose a more secure covert scheme, where a multiple antennas transmitter assisted by a multi-antenna UAV jammer maximizes the covert secrecy rate under the scenarios of both correct and incorrect detection by a warden with both error detection probability and eavesdropping rate limitations satisfied. The transmitter and jammer adopt maximum ratio transmission (MRT) and zero-forcing to maximize the transmission rate and minimize the interference at the receiver, respectively. First, we analyze the monotonicity of error detection probability to determine the optimal power detection threshold and the corresponding largest error detection probability. Then, under this worst case, we jointly optimize the transmit and jamming power to maximize the covert secrecy rate while guaranteeing the covert and eavesdropping limits meet their respective requirements. Finally, simulation results are presented to prove the correctness of the theoretical conclusion and evaluate the effectiveness of our proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Industrial Semantic Communications for Tool Wear Monitoring in Industrial IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an Industrial Semantic Communications (ISC) framework to ensure efficient and in-telligent communication in Industrial Internet-of-Things (IIoT) networks, and further apply the proposed framework to the task of tool wear monitoring. A semantic-aware tool wear monitoring network (TWM-Net) is designed to accurately identify the idling state from tool wear data, thus assisting the semantic data transmission process of the ISC framework. Then, a demo software system is implemented to verify the delay performance of the proposed ISC framework. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed ISC framework can facilitate the semantic information exchange between edge industrial system and cloud platform together with the deep compressed sensing method, and significantly reduce the amount of data transmissions in IIoT networks. The source code and dataset is available through https://github.com/pnixsoft/TWM-Net.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Trajectory Design and Computing Offloading in UAV-Aided IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we propose to minimize the total energy expenditure in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) internet of things (loT) networks by employing the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). Considering the obstacles of an urban city environment, a composite optimization model incorporating both the flight trajectory and computational offloading is initially formulated. To address this non-convex problem, the original problem is converted into two independent subproblems, and then an energy-efficient trajectory design and computing offloading algorithm is developed by employing the successive convex approximation (SCA) and quadratic approximation approaches. Moreover, comprehensive simulation results verify that the proposed algorithm achieves a decrease in weighted energy expenditure by 14.8% in comparison to the algorithms employing a fixed trajectory, fixed transmit power, and the orthogonal multiple access (OMA).

articleTitle: Sensing for 6G Metaverse: Intelligent Target Clustering and Spectrum Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Recently, radar-like sensing systems are expected to be key pillars of the 6G wireless network. Suffering from congested electromagnetic spectrum, multiple radars can coordi-nate frequency utilization and target allocation, so as to mitigate mutual interference and enhance detection performance. Focusing on the scenario of multiple frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radars, this paper proposes an autonomous target clustering and subband configuration scheme, where we model the complex decision-making problem with different time scales of the radar system as semi-Markov decision process (SMDP), which is transformed into a hierarchical decision-making structure with beam direction decision-making problem and the problem on selection of the subband and chirp rate, avoiding the stacking of action space dimensions. With the aim of tackling the challenge of multi-targets allocation, task cognition-driven target clustering is achieved through graph convolutional network (GCN) to provide accurate clustering results for radars. To learn policies, an actor-critic algorithm combined with GCN based on hierarchical reinforcement learning is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively reduce interference between radars and assist radar systems in accurately detecting targets, with the target claustering method effectively enhancing the algorithm's performance.

articleTitle: Experimental Implementation of an OTFS-Based ISAC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) possesses unique advantages in high-mobility communication scenar-ios due to its robustness against high Doppler frequency shifts, making it an ideal modulation technique for Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) to achieve target sensing functionality. Current research on OTFS for target localization is primarily based on simulations, and the advantages of OTFS signals in target localization have not been fully exploited. Therefore, this paper proposes a three-ellipse positioning algorithm, combined with an off-grid channel estimation method, to achieve the OTFS signal target positioning function. We use the embedded pilot-assisted channel estimation scheme of OTFS to insert pilots, data symbols, and protection areas in the delayed-Doppler plane. Then, the delay and Doppler information of the channel are estimated by the pilot position in the received signal to obtain the physical properties of the channel, including distance, velocity, etc. The three-ellipse positioning algorithm is used to estimate the target position based on these channel parameters. Finally, we build a real communication scenario and our algorithm was experimentally verified by using a USRP-based software defined radio (SDR) platform, proving the effectiveness of our algorithm on the hardware platform.

articleTitle: Super-Resolution Sparse Bayesian Learning-Based Channel Estimation in Bistatic Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: For bistatic sensing, the accuracy of the channel estimation will largely affect the accuracy of the sensing parameters. The traditional sparse recovery-based channel estimation scheme suffers from severe resolution loss due to the angle quantization of the channel. To improve the channel estimation accuracy, this paper proposes a channel estimation scheme based on super-resolution sparse Bayesian learning (SBL). The scheme pre-candidates part of the angular domain grid through preprocessing, and iteratively shifts the estimated angle of arrival (AoA) /angle of departure (AoD) towards the optimal solution by root SBL of the Kronecker sparse structure of the cascaded channel, which eventually realizes the super-resolution channel estimation. Simulation results verify that this scheme has better performance than the conventional solutions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sampling for Real-Time Status Update Systems under Non-Stationary Delay Statistics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/CIC International Conference on Communications in China (ICCC Workshops)
abstract: In this paper, we study the sampling rate design problem of status update systems under unknown and non-stationary delay statistics, where the delay statistics include both the distribution of transmission delay and the packet loss probability. When the delay statistics are non-stationary, short-term average Age-of-Information (AoI) is much more critical than the long-term average AoI. Motivated by this fact, we formulate a sampling rate control problem by minimizing the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of the average AoI in each control cycle to a predefined AoI target, such that both the short-term and long-term average AoI approach to the target. The formulated problem is different from the existing works on the minimization of long-term average AoI under known or stationary delay statistics. Based on the average AoI feedback at the end of each control cycle, we first present a Delta Sampling (DS) policy with a fixed updating step. Because the DS policy may converge slowly, we then propose a novel Adaptive Sampling Control (ASC) policy to adjust the sampling rate dynamically. The main challenge in developing ASC is the lack of an explicit model to reflect the relationship between the sampling rate and average AoI. To overcome this issue, we design an equivalent dynamic linearization data model with a Pseudo-Partial Derivative (PPD), where the unknown features of delay statistics can be captured by the time-varying PPD. By estimating the PPD in each control cycle, ASC can determine a suitable sampling rate based on the tractable data model. Numerical results show that the proposed ASC policy outperforms the DS, zero waiting, and fixed sampling policies significantly in terms of MSE by more than 100% under unknown and non-stationary delay statistics.
